sections.subtitle: Prvi u Europskoj uniji po višku kilograma: kada kuhanje postane vikend-luksuz
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava da se u Hrvatskoj premalo kuha i previše poseže za gotovom hranom
sections.content:
Razgovor počinje podatkom koji nikoga ne ostavlja ravnodušnim. Voditelj podsjeća profesoricu **Donatellu Verbanac** da je Hrvatska prva u Europskoj uniji po udjelu ljudi s viškom kilograma i pita gdje se pogriješilo. Gošća priznaje da joj je to „jako čudno“. Podsjeća da je u proteklim desetljećima osnovano mnogo povjerenstava koja su zagovarala pravilnu prehranu. U jednom od njih i sama je sjedila prije više od 25 godina. Ipak, naglašava da **debljina nije stvar samo kalorija**.

Problem vidi na razini cijele populacije, nažalost i djece. Ljudi sve češće traže jednostavna rješenja, **premalo kuhaju** i sve više koriste gotovu hranu. Užurbani način života i svojevrsno blagostanje to dodatno potiču. Ilustrira to podatkom da prosječna velika trgovina prehrambenih proizvoda može imati i do **300.000 različitih artikala**, pa je izbor golem.

Gošća se vraća na misao iz njihova prethodnog razgovora: namirnice treba jesti onakve kakve one zaista jesu, nativne. „Ako je banana, banana. Ako je mlijeko, mlijeko“, kaže ona. Kada se takva hrana polako žvače, stvara se osjećaj ugode i svjesnosti o jedenju. Sitost se tada javlja otprilike **20 minuta nakon obroka**. Brzinsko jedenje i ispijanje pića s velikim količinama šećera, upozorava, stvara pikove glukoze, a zatim i pikove inzulina. Zbog toga se glad vrlo brzo vraća.

Hrvatska u tome nije iznimka. Slične trendove među mlađom populacijom i školskom djecom bilježe razvijeni dijelovi Italije, ali i dijelovi nekoć slabije ekonomske moći. Ondje je debljina postala sve veći problem upravo zato što je procesirana hrana jeftina i dostupna. Riječ je o grickalicama, konzervama, sokovima u tetrapaku i slatkim mliječnim napitcima. Kao primjer navodi pakiranja od desetak do dvanaest kroasana koji nisu tek ispečeni, nego sadrže brojne aditive. Takva su pakiranja nekad postojala samo u Americi kao „king size“ proizvodi. Uz njih se često piju takozvani voćni sokovi prepuni šećera.

Najveći problem ipak vidi u tome što su ljudi prestali kuhati. Kuhanje je, kaže, postalo **luksuz rezerviran za vikend**. Smatra da bi u hrvatskoj kulturi ono trebalo biti svakodnevica i prvi način obrane od gotove hrane, preko koje se unose tvari koje tijelu mogu itekako zasmetati.
sections.subtitle_en: First in the European Union in excess weight: when cooking becomes a weekend luxury
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains that people cook too little and rely too much on convenience food in Croatia
sections.content_en:
The conversation begins with a piece of information that leaves no one indifferent. The host reminds Professor **Donatella Verbanac** that Croatia is first in the European Union in the share of people with excess weight and asks where things went wrong. The guest admits that this is "very strange" to her. She recalls that numerous committees advocating proper nutrition were established in past decades. She herself sat on one of them more than 25 years ago. Still, she emphasizes that **obesity is not just a matter of calories**.

She sees the problem at the level of the entire population, unfortunately including children. People increasingly look for simple solutions, **cook too little**, and use ready-made food more and more. A hectic lifestyle and a kind of affluence further encourage this. She illustrates this with the fact that an average large grocery store can have up to **300,000 different items**, making the choice enormous.

The guest returns to a thought from their previous conversation: groceries should be eaten the way they truly are, native. "If it's a banana, banana. If it's milk, milk," she says. When such food is chewed slowly, a feeling of pleasure and awareness of eating is created. Satiety then occurs approximately **20 minutes after a meal**. Eating quickly and drinking beverages with large amounts of sugar, she warns, creates glucose spikes, followed by insulin spikes. Because of that, hunger returns very quickly.

Croatia is no exception in this. Similar trends among the younger population and school children are recorded in developed parts of Italy, but also in parts that once had weaker economic power. There, obesity has become an increasing problem precisely because processed food is cheap and accessible. We are talking about snacks, canned goods, juice cartons, and sweetened dairy drinks. As an example, she mentions packages of ten to twelve croissants that are not freshly baked, but contain numerous additives. Such packages once existed only in America as "king size" products. Alongside them, so-called fruit juices packed with sugar are often drunk.

Yet she sees the greatest problem in the fact that people have stopped cooking. Cooking, she says, has become a **luxury reserved for the weekend**. She believes that in Croatian culture it should be an everyday occurrence and the first line of defense against ready-made food, through which substances are introduced that can thoroughly bother the body.

sections.subtitle: Volja ili biologija: debljina je bolest sa svojom šifrom
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava kada je debljina dobila dijagnostičku šifru i zašto se toliko čekalo
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim iskreno priznaje vlastitu zabludu. Nekad je ljude s viškom kilograma znao isključivo osuđivati. Govorio je da je to pitanje njihove discipline i volje, uz savjet „zatvori malo usta, nemoj previše jesti“. Pita je li to doista tako jednostavno i kakva je uloga hormona u tijelu.

Donatella Verbanac potvrđuje da je društvo dugo osuđivalo pretile ljude. Smatralo ih se osobama koje jedu sve što im padne pod ruku, nemaju „higijenu jedenja“ i ne žele se kretati ni trošiti kalorije. „I bili smo u krivu, sto posto u krivu“, poručuje ona.

Debljina je kao bolest dobila šifru pod **slovom E**. Gošća se prisjeća da se to dogodilo oko 2004. ili 2005. godine, a točan broj šifre ne navodi sa sigurnošću. Bez dodijeljene šifre ne može se postaviti dijagnoza. Kao razlog dugog čekanja navodi situaciju u Americi, gdje je debljina „galopirala“. Dijagnoza bi određenim ljudima dala pravo na liječenje, a to bi stvorilo velik pritisak na socijalni i zdravstveni sustav.

Regulatorna i zakonodavna tijela ipak nisu mogla sakriti činjenice. Tada se počelo govoriti i o **epigenetici**. Prema riječima gošće, geni su tek „municija“, a životni stil i okolnosti u kojima se čovjek razvija određuju kako se geni eksprimiraju u proteine. Ti su čimbenici čak važniji od samih gena. Svoju misao sažima u jednu rečenicu: **„Životni stil je okidač, a geni su municija.“**
sections.subtitle_en: Willpower or biology: obesity is a disease with its own code
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains when obesity received a diagnostic code and why the wait was so long
sections.content_en:
The host then candidly admits his own misconception. He used to exclusively judge people with excess weight. He would say it was a question of their discipline and willpower, along with the advice "close your mouth a bit, don't eat too much." He asks whether it is really that simple and what role hormones play in the body.

Donatella Verbanac confirms that society judged obese people for a long time. They were considered persons who eat whatever falls into their hands, lack "eating hygiene," and do not want to move or burn calories. "And we were wrong, one hundred percent wrong," she conveys.

Obesity as a disease received a code under the **letter E**. The guest recalls that this happened around 2004 or 2005, and she does not state the exact number of the code with certainty. Without an assigned code, a diagnosis cannot be made. As a reason for the long wait, she cites the situation in America, where obesity was "galloping." A diagnosis would grant certain people the right to treatment, and that would create great pressure on the social and healthcare system.

Yet regulatory and legislative bodies could not hide the facts. That was when people also began talking about **epigenetics**. In the guest's words, genes are merely "ammunition," while lifestyle and the circumstances under which a person develops determine how genes are expressed into proteins. These factors are even more important than the genes themselves. She summarizes her thought in one sentence: **"Lifestyle is the trigger, and genes are the ammunition."**

sections.subtitle: Nizozemska glad 1944.: kada glad bake određuje kilograme unuka
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac opisuje nizozemsku glad 1944. i praćenje potomaka trudnica
sections.content:
Kao primjer epigenetskog utjecaja gošća navodi studiju objavljenu u Nizozemskoj 70-ih godina. Priznaje da ni sama dugo nije znala za nju. Studija je proučavala posljedice **velike nizozemske gladi 1944. godine**, predzadnje godine rata, kada su se njemačke trupe već povlačile. Hrane nije bilo, kanali su bili zaleđeni, a izuzetno teška glad trajala je otprilike šest mjeseci ili dulje. Izračunato je da su ljudi tada jeli najviše oko **100 kilokalorija dnevno**. Gošća to slikovito uspoređuje: jedna banana ima „90 i nešto“ kilokalorija.

Znanstvenici su pratili dvije generacije potomaka žena koje su tijekom gladi bile u prvom ili drugom tromjesečju trudnoće. U generacijama koje su uslijedile zabilježen je **velik porast debljine**. Ta djeca nisu jednostavno jela puno, nego su bila **predisponirana da jedu puno**. Kasnije su utvrđene promjene u epigenetici, odnosno dokazane **metilacijske promjene**. Iscrpljeni organizam majke nije imao dovoljno kalorija za razvoj ploda. Zato se dogodila promjena koja je „to čedo“ pripremila da kasnije stvara rezerve. Ista se sklonost prenijela i na njegovu djecu.

Voditelj zaključuje da je riječ o dubljoj biološkoj razini, a gošća to potvrđuje. Epigenetske promjene mogu se naslijediti od djedova, pa čak i pradjedova. Oprezno dodaje da te osobe ne bi nazvala pretilima jer ne poznaje sve podatke. Ipak, u usporedbi s prosječnim stanovništvom Nizozemske iste dobi, potomci nizozemske gladi imali su **veću tjelesnu masu i sklonost nakupljanju masnog tkiva**.

Na pitanje je li to povezano s hormonima, odgovara da jest, ali i s cjelokupnom biokemijom organizma. Generacije F1 i F2, djeca i unuci, dobile su kroz epigenetske promjene točno određen kemijski signal. Taj im je signal nalagao da u organizmu steknu dovoljno rezervi za slučaj nove gladi.
sections.subtitle_en: The Dutch famine of 1944: when a grandmother's hunger determines the grandchild's kilograms
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac describes the Dutch famine of 1944 and tracking the offspring of pregnant women
sections.content_en:
As an example of epigenetic influence, the guest cites a study published in the Netherlands in the 1970s. She admits that she herself did not know about it for a long time. The study investigated the consequences of the **great Dutch famine of 1944**, the penultimate year of the war, when German troops were already retreating. There was no food, the canals were frozen, and an extremely severe famine lasted about six months or longer. It was calculated that people then ate at most about **100 kilocalories a day**. The guest vividly compares this: one banana has "90-something" kilocalories.

Scientists tracked two generations of offspring of women who were in their first or second trimester of pregnancy during the famine. In the generations that followed, a **large increase in obesity** was recorded. Those children did not simply eat a lot, but were **predisposed to eat a lot**. Later, changes in epigenetics were established, namely proven **methylation changes**. The mother's exhausted organism did not have enough calories for fetal development. Therefore, a change occurred that prepared "that infant" to build reserves later. The same tendency was passed on to their children as well.

The host concludes that this is a deeper biological level, and the guest confirms this. Epigenetic changes can be inherited from grandfathers, and even great-grandfathers. She cautiously adds that she would not call these individuals obese because she does not know all the data. Still, compared to the average population of the Netherlands of the same age, the descendants of the Dutch famine had **greater body weight and a tendency to accumulate fatty tissue**.

To the question of whether this is related to hormones, she answers that it is, but also to the overall biochemistry of the organism. Generations F1 and F2, children and grandchildren, received a precise chemical signal through epigenetic changes. That signal instructed them to acquire enough reserves in the body in case of a new famine.

sections.subtitle: Je li rat devedesetih ostavio trag na kilogramima Hrvata?
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća razmišlja o mogućoj poveznici ratnih devedesetih i današnje debljine
sections.content:
Voditelj pita može li se nizozemsko iskustvo povezati s današnjim stanjem u Hrvatskoj. Donatella Verbanac kaže da odgovor ne zna, ali kolegama želi „staviti bubu u uho“. Prije tridesetak godina, u ratno vrijeme, i sami su ljudi ovdje bili prisiljeni na odricanje. Prisjeća se da su dohodci pali na **petinu uobičajenih mjesečnih primanja**, a vladala je i nestašica hrane. Devedesete su bile izazovne i teške godine za sve. Današnje stanje, smatra, **može biti i posljedica toga**.

Zato posebno cijeni što se 2002. i 2003. na razini ministarstava počelo raditi na **povjerenstvu za pravilnu prehranu** i praćenju stanja. Tu akciju smatra iznimno vrijednom i potrebnom. Upozoravanja treba razvijati stalno i istim intenzitetom. Na ovom podneblju, naglašava, postoje svi uvjeti za kvalitetnu prehranu i kvalitetne namirnice.
sections.subtitle_en: Did the war in the nineties leave a mark on Croats' kilograms?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest ponders a possible link between the wartime nineties and today's obesity
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether the Dutch experience can be connected to today's situation in Croatia. Donatella Verbanac says she does not know the answer, but wants to "put a bug in the ear" of her colleagues. About thirty years ago, during wartime, people here were themselves forced to make sacrifices. She recalls that incomes fell to **one-fifth of customary monthly earnings**, and food shortages prevailed. The nineties were challenging and difficult years for everyone. Today's situation, she believes, **could also be a consequence of that**.

That is why she particularly appreciates that in 2002 and 2003, at the ministerial level, work began on a **proper nutrition committee** and monitoring the situation. She considers that initiative extremely valuable and necessary. Warnings should be developed constantly and with the same intensity. In this region, she emphasizes, all conditions exist for high-quality nutrition and high-quality ingredients.

sections.subtitle: Jadranska, a ne mediteranska prehrana: zašto bi Sardinija bila plava zona, a Hrvatska ne?
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava pojam jadranske prehrane
sections.content:
Gošća nabraja čime ovo podneblje raspolaže: voćem, povrćem, ribom, mesom i dobrim mlijekom. Tko ne jede meso, ovdje može nabaviti vrlo kvalitetne mahunarke. Zato za ovaj dio Sredozemlja uvijek koristi pojam **jadranska, a ne mediteranska prehrana**. Ovdje se koriste neke namirnice koje, primjerice, sjeverna Afrika kao dio Mediterana ne koristi ili ih koristi drukčije.

Grana jadranske prehrane, prema njezinim riječima, obuhvaća:
- **Italiju**
- **Hrvatsku**
- **Crnu Goru**
- **Albaniju**
- **dio Bosne**

U tim krajevima postoji duga tradicija kvalitetne i jednostavne hrane. Zato se, kaže, ne treba ugledati na Sardiniju. „Zašto bi Sardinija bila **blue zone** i longevity zona kad mi tako jedemo isto?“, pita se.

Žali što su variva i jušna jela „na žlicu“ gotovo nestala. Ljudi kao da su zaboravili da je to najjednostavniji način da u hladnjaku uvijek ima hrane koja se brzo pripremi i od koje je čovjek sit.
sections.subtitle_en: Adriatic, not Mediterranean diet: why would Sardinia be a blue zone, and Croatia not?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains the concept of the Adriatic diet
sections.content_en:
The guest lists what this region has at its disposal: fruit, vegetables, fish, meat, and good milk. Whoever does not eat meat can obtain very high-quality legumes here. Therefore, for this part of the Mediterranean, she always uses the term **Adriatic, not Mediterranean diet**. Certain foods are used here that, for instance, North Africa as part of the Mediterranean does not use or uses differently.

The Adriatic diet branch, according to her words, encompasses:
- **Italy**
- **Croatia**
- **Montenegro**
- **Albania**
- **part of Bosnia**

In these regions, there is a long tradition of high-quality and simple food. Therefore, she says, one should not look up to Sardinia. "Why would Sardinia be a **blue zone** and longevity zone when we eat like that too?", she wonders.

She regrets that stews and soupy dishes "eaten with a spoon" have almost vanished. It is as if people have forgotten that this is the simplest way to always have food in the refrigerator that is prepared quickly and that keeps a person full.

sections.subtitle: Prvih pet godina života: majčina variva iz Slavonije kao najbolji zalog
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava razvoj masnih stanica u prvih pet godina života na primjeru voditeljeva djetinjstva
sections.content:
Voditelj se prepoznaje u opisu jušnih jela jer ga je majka upravo tako hranila. Otkako je otišao „iz gnijezda“, hrani se drukčije. Kaže da ga je uhvatio brzi životni stil: nema vremena, a kako se radi jedna stvar, tako se rade sve, pa i jelo.

Donatella Verbanac odgovara da je očito imao jako dobre temelje. **Broj masnih stanica razvija se ponajviše tijekom prvih pet godina života**, pa je prehrana u tom razdoblju izuzetno važna. Voditelj potvrđuje da je odrastao u Slavoniji, gdje je mama kuhala „sve jušno“ i variva. Gošća zaključuje da je hrana pripremljena na jednostavan način, uz začine i povrće, ostavila trag u njegovim stanicama, hormonima i **mikrobioti**. Upravo zato, smatra, danas nije sklon nekontroliranom debljanju.

Voditelj dodaje da je godište 1985. Kad je rat počeo, bio je dijete. Smatra da su svi na ovim prostorima, „i Hrvati i Bosanci i Srbi i Slovenci“, ratom bili zahvaćeni i psihološki te da je on na svima ostavio posljedice.
sections.subtitle_en: First five years of life: mother's stews from Slavonija as the best pledge
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the development of fat cells in the first five years of life using the host's childhood as an example
sections.content_en:
The host recognizes himself in the description of soupy dishes because his mother fed him exactly like that. Ever since he left "the nest," he eats differently. He says a fast lifestyle has caught up with him: there is no time, and as one does one thing, so one does everything, including eating.

Donatella Verbanac replies that he obviously had very good foundations. **The number of fat cells develops mostly during the first five years of life**, so nutrition in that period is exceptionally important. The host confirms that he grew up in Slavonija, where mom cooked "everything soupy" and stews. The guest concludes that food prepared in a simple manner, with spices and vegetables, left a mark in his cells, hormones, and **microbiota**. Precisely because of that, she believes, he is not prone to uncontrolled weight gain today.

The host adds that he was born in 1985. When the war started, he was a child. He believes that everyone in these territories, "both Croats and Bosnians and Serbs and Slovenes," were affected by the war psychologically as well, and that it left consequences on everyone.

sections.subtitle: Od odgovornosti do endokrinologije: što su zapravo hormoni
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac biokemijski definira hormone i endokrine žlijezde
sections.content:
Voditelj predlaže da se epigenetske i duboke biološke posljedice ostave po strani jer na njih više nije moguće utjecati. Politiku želi izbjeći. Razgovor usmjerava na ono gdje je moguće **preuzeti odgovornost**: na hormone. Pita što su hormoni i koji su važni za prehranu.

Gošća ih biokemijski definira kao **kemijske molekule koje izlučuju žlijezde u organizmu**. Krv ih zatim prenosi do ciljnih stanica. Iz toga se razvila cijela znanost **endokrinologije**, koja proučava endokrine žlijezde i njihove izlučevine.

Teško je reći koji je hormon najvažniji. Stručnjaci bi, kaže, na prvo mjesto stavili hormone **hipotalamusa**. Hipotalamus zapravo ne luči same hormone, nego čimbenike koji potiču njihovo otpuštanje u krv. Drugi bi pak istaknuli **hormone štitnjače**.
sections.subtitle_en: From responsibility to endocrinology: what hormones actually are
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac biochemically defines hormones and endocrine glands
sections.content_en:
The host proposes leaving epigenetic and deep biological consequences aside because they can no longer be influenced. He wants to avoid politics. He directs the conversation toward where it is possible to **take responsibility**: to hormones. He asks what hormones are and which ones are important for nutrition.

The guest biochemically defines them as **chemical molecules secreted by glands in the body**. Blood then transports them to target cells. From this developed the entire science of **endocrinology**, which studies endocrine glands and their secretions.

It is difficult to say which hormone is the most important. Experts, she says, would place the hormones of the **hypothalamus** in first place. The hypothalamus does not actually secrete the hormones themselves, but rather factors that stimulate their release into the blood. Others, on the other hand, would highlight **thyroid hormones**.

sections.subtitle: Jod, sol i ioni: sitni atomi koji drže organizam u ravnoteži
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava ulogu joda u sintezi hormona štitnjače
sections.content:
Kao primjer dobre javnozdravstvene odluke gošća ističe rad endokrinologa i internista u Hrvatskoj i na širem području. Oni su uočili da se golema većina ljudi suočavala s **nedostatkom joda**, pa se počela **jodirati kamena sol**. Spominje razdoblje od 60-ih do 80-ih godina, kada mnogi nisu dobivali dovoljno joda.

Bez dovoljno joda u hrani nema ni dovoljno joda za sintezu hormona štitnjače. To pokazuju već i njihova imena:
- **trijodtironin** ima tri atoma joda,
- **tetrajodtironin, odnosno tiroksin**, ima četiri atoma joda.

Na pitanje zašto je jod toliko važan, gošća odgovara da može posuđivati elektrone kad je potrebno. „Sve je to stvar fizike na kraju“, kaže, odnosno otpuštanja i primanja elektrona. Na sličan su način za organizam važni i drugi elementi. Klor navodi kao glavni stanični anion, natrij kao glavni vanstanični kation, a kalij kao glavni stanični kation. Ravnoteža tih naboja, zaključuje, jest ravnoteža organizma.

Zatim spominje gušteraču, koja je postala vrlo zanimljiva zbog inzulina i glukagona. Zanimanje su potaknuli i lijekovi koji djeluju na njihove receptore i pomažu pri mršavljenju.
sections.subtitle_en: Iodine, salt, and ions: tiny atoms that keep the organism in balance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the role of iodine in the synthesis of thyroid hormones
sections.content_en:
As an example of a good public health decision, the guest highlights the work of endocrinologists and internists in Croatia and the wider region. They observed that the vast majority of people were facing **iodine deficiency**, so **rock salt began to be iodized**. She mentions the period from the 1960s to the 1980s, when many did not receive enough iodine.

Without enough iodine in food, there is also not enough iodine for the synthesis of thyroid hormones. Their names already show this:
- **triiodothyronine** has three iodine atoms,
- **tetraiodothyronine, that is thyroxine**, has four iodine atoms.

When asked why iodine is so important, the guest replies that it can lend electrons when necessary. "It's all a matter of physics in the end," she says, namely the release and acceptance of electrons. In a similar way, other elements are also important for the organism. She cites chloride as the main cellular anion, sodium as the main extracellular cation, and potassium as the main cellular cation. The balance of these charges, she concludes, is the balance of the organism.

Then she mentions the pancreas, which has become very interesting due to insulin and glucagon. Interest was also sparked by drugs that act on their receptors and aid in weight loss.

sections.subtitle: Orkestar s dirigentom, a štitnjača svira bas: kako nastaje gušavost
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac uspoređuje hormone s orkestrom
sections.content:
Hormone Donatella Verbanac studentima često objašnjava kao **glazbenike u orkestru**. Postoji i središnji dirigent. Je li to neka žlijezda ili mozak, prepušta onima koji to najbolje znaju. Kada je orkestar uigran, čuje se predivna melodija. Ako bilo koji član ne svira prema notama, to se osjeti, a u organizmu se tada javlja **neravnoteža**.

Kada nedostaje joda, nema dovoljno supstrata za sintezu hormona štitnjače. Štitnjača tada pokušava proizvesti što više stanica i maksimalno narasti kako bi nadoknadila manjak. Hormoni štitnjače određuju **anabolizam i katabolizam**, odnosno ugradnju i razgradnju tvari. Zato ih uspoređuje s **bas gitarom**, koja daje ritam cijelom orkestru.

Posljedica manjka joda je **gušavost**. Ta je jednostavna bolest ovdje nekad bila sasvim uobičajena, a rješava se jednostavno, uvođenjem joda u prehranu. Voditelj zaključuje da se zato i počela jodirati sol. Gošća dodaje da se u Engleskoj sol ni danas ne jodira jer ondje smatraju da imaju dovoljno joda iz drugih namirnica i drugih vrsta soli. Engleska je poznata po dobroj soli, poput maldonske i keltske. Na ovim se prostorima jodiranje uvelo preventivno. Za to su najzaslužniji ljudi koji su tada radili, a među njima je bio i **akademik Kusić**.

Voditelj se čudi koliko naizgled jednostavni spojevi utječu na organizam. Gošća objašnjava da se hormoni luče u vrlo malim količinama. Koliko će ih biti u krvi, određuje to koliko ih ciljna stanica treba ili može primiti.
sections.subtitle_en: An orchestra with a conductor, and the thyroid plays bass: how goiter occurs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac compares hormones to an orchestra
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac often explains hormones to students as **musicians in an orchestra**. There is also a central conductor. Whether that is some gland or the brain, she leaves to those who know best. When the orchestra is well-rehearsed, a wonderful melody is heard. If any member does not play according to the notes, it is felt, and an **imbalance** then occurs in the organism.

When iodine is lacking, there is not enough substrate for the synthesis of thyroid hormones. The thyroid gland then tries to produce as many cells as possible and grow to the maximum to compensate for the deficiency. Thyroid hormones determine **anabolism and catabolism**, that is, the incorporation and breakdown of substances. That is why she compares them to a **bass guitar**, which provides the rhythm for the entire orchestra.

A consequence of iodine deficiency is **goiter**. This simple disease was once quite common here, and it is resolved simply, by introducing iodine into the diet. The host concludes that this is why salt began to be iodized. The guest adds that in England salt is still not iodized today because they believe they have enough iodine from other foods and other types of salt. England is known for good salt, such as Maldon and Celtic. In this region, iodization was introduced preventively. Most credited for this are the people who worked back then, and among them was **Academician Kusić**.

The host marvels at how much seemingly simple compounds influence the organism. The guest explains that hormones are secreted in very small amounts. How much of them will be in the blood is determined by how much the target cell needs or can receive.

sections.subtitle: Kortizol nije samo zločesti hormon: bez njega ne bismo pobjegli morskom psu
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava da je kortizol potreban u situacijama opasnosti
sections.content:
Gošća hormone dijeli u dvije glavne skupine. Prvu čine **steroidni hormoni**, molekule s kondenziranim prstenovima. Luče ih uglavnom **nadbubrežna žlijezda** i **spolne žlijezde**. Riječ je o spolnim hormonima i hormonima kore nadbubrežne žlijezde.

Ključna je činjenica, naglašava, da se oni **sintetiziraju iz kolesterola**. Tko ne unosi dovoljno masti i kolesterola, neće imati normalne funkcije ni na razini sinteze **kortizola**. Za kortizol se kaže da je „zločesti hormon“, no gošća tvrdi da to nije tako. Bez njega čovjek ne bi pobjegao kad za njim pliva morski pas. Kortizol, zajedno s adrenalinom i glukagonom, omogućuje brzo oslobađanje glukoze u krv kad je potrebno.

Problem nastaje kad ga je previše. Njegova prirodna razina najviša je pred jutro, kako bi čovjek s izlaskom sunca imao snage i volje krenuti u novi dan. Ako je kortizol stalno visok, to znači **kronični stres** i neprekidno prekomjerno opterećenje nadbubrežne žlijezde.
sections.subtitle_en: Cortisol is not just a naughty hormone: without it we wouldn't escape a shark
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that cortisol is needed in dangerous situations
sections.content_en:
The guest divides hormones into two main groups. The first consists of **steroid hormones**, molecules with condensed rings. They are mainly secreted by the **adrenal gland** and the **gonads**. These are sex hormones and hormones of the adrenal cortex.

A crucial fact, she emphasizes, is that they are **synthesized from cholesterol**. Whoever does not consume enough fats and cholesterol will not have normal functions even at the level of **cortisol** synthesis. Cortisol is said to be a "naughty hormone," but the guest claims that this is not so. Without it, a person would not escape when a shark is swimming after them. Cortisol, together with adrenaline and glucagon, enables the rapid release of glucose into the blood when needed.

The problem arises when there is too much of it. Its natural level is highest toward morning, so that a person, with the sunrise, has the strength and willpower to start a new day. If cortisol is constantly high, that means **chronic stress** and continuous overload of the adrenal gland.

sections.subtitle: Hormoni nisu ženska tema: andropauza i rastuća muška neplodnost
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava da spolni hormoni postoje kod oba spola
sections.content:
Bez dovoljno kolesterola nema ni normalne sinteze **estrogena, progesterona i testosterona**, upozorava gošća. Naglašava da svi ti hormoni postoje i u muškom i u ženskom organizmu, samo u različitim količinama.

Kaže da se o hormonima nekad uvijek govorilo kao o „ženskoj temi“. Povezivali su se s mjesečnim ciklusom od 28 dana i pripremom maternice za oplodnju. Ako do nje ne dođe, nastupa krvarenje, a s njim promjene raspoloženja i sna. Hormoni su se povezivali sa ženama i kod ulaska u menopauzu.

Danas se zna i za **andropauzu**. Gošća priznaje da o njoj ne zna previše. Predlaže da se u podcast pozove stručnjak iz reproduktivne medicine. On bi mogao objasniti što sve, kao **endogeni disruptori**, smanjuje količinu muških hormona. Danas je, ističe, **neplodnost kod muškaraca velika**.
sections.subtitle_en: Hormones are not a female topic: andropause and rising male infertility
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains that sex hormones exist in both sexes
sections.content_en:
Without enough cholesterol, there is also no normal synthesis of **estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone**, the guest warns. She emphasizes that all these hormones exist in both the male and female organisms, just in different quantities.

She says that hormones used to always be spoken of as a "female topic." They were associated with the 28-day monthly cycle and the preparation of the uterus for fertilization. If it does not occur, bleeding ensues, and with it changes in mood and sleep. Hormones were also associated with women upon entering menopause.

Today, **andropause** is also known. The guest admits that she does not know too much about it. She suggests inviting an expert in reproductive medicine to the podcast. He could explain what all, as **endocrine disruptors**, reduces the amount of male hormones. Today, she points out, **infertility in men is high**.

sections.subtitle: Jod iz morskog zraka i zašto su hormoni ipak dijelom krivi
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća potvrđuje da u izjavi ‘krivi su hormoni’ ima istine i ističe ulogu endokrinologa
sections.content:
Vraćajući se jodu, Donatella Verbanac navodi da se njegov nedostatak može riješiti morskom soli ili boravkom uz more jer ga **ima mnogo i u aerosolu**. Tko živi blizu mora, jede dosta ribe i bilje koje raste uz obalu, dobiva dovoljno joda. Problem su uvijek bili **kontinentalni dijelovi zemlje**, gdje se koristila kamena sol i jod se nije mogao nadoknaditi.

Voditelj sažima: ima li istine u izjavi „krivi su hormoni“? Gošća potvrđuje da ima. Kod svakog čovjeka treba pogledati **endokrinološku sliku**. Endokrinolozi, ističe, vrlo dobro znaju kako **titrirati** određene hormone i uvesti ih u svakodnevnu primjenu. Kada se manjak nadoknadi, metabolizam se itekako dobro uspostavi.
sections.subtitle_en: Iodine from sea air and why hormones are still partly to blame
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest confirms that there is truth in the statement 'hormones are to blame' and highlights the role of endocrinologists
sections.content_en:
Returning to iodine, Donatella Verbanac states that its deficiency can be resolved with sea salt or staying near the sea because **there is a lot of it in aerosols as well**. Whoever lives near the sea, eats plenty of fish and herbs growing along the coast, gets enough iodine. The problem was always the **continental parts of the country**, where rock salt was used and iodine could not be compensated.

The host summarizes: is there truth in the statement "hormones are to blame"? The guest confirms that there is. In every person, one should look at the **endocrinological picture**. Endocrinologists, she points out, know very well how to **titrate** certain hormones and introduce them into daily use. When the deficit is compensated, metabolism is established very well indeed.

sections.subtitle: Inzulin živi dvije minute: kako slatki zalogaji iscrpljuju gušteraču
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac otkriva da je poluvrijeme inzulina u krvi oko dvije minute
sections.content:
Na pitanje koji su hormoni vezani uz glad i sitost, gošća najavljuje hormon o kojemu se u njezino studentsko doba gotovo nije govorilo. Prije toga objašnjava **inzulin**. Inzulin je **peptidni hormon**, građen od aminokiselina poput bjelančevina, za razliku od steroidnih hormona. Razlika je bitna jer peptidne hormone u krvi brzo razgrađuju enzimi proteaze.

Zatim voditelju postavlja pitanje: koliko je poluvrijeme života inzulina u krvi? On nagađa oko šest sati. Odgovor ga iznenađuje: **oko dvije minute, ili još manje**. Hormoni su kemijski glasnici koji samo trebaju pokrenuti reakciju. Inzulin odmah reagira na porast glukoze nakon obroka, odnosno postprandijalno.

Gošća zatim opisuje svakodnevni scenarij. Netko pojede pakiranu torticu u celofanu ili suhi kolačić sa slatkim dodatkom i uz to popije limenku ili tetrapak soka. Glukoza mu tada vrlo brzo poraste. Granice u kojima glukoza mora biti u krvi vrlo su uske, grubo **od 3 do 5 milimola po litri**. Sve iznad toga ne valja. No ni pad ispod 3 nije bezopasan jer bez dovoljno glukoze čovjek može umrijeti. **Mozak i srce troše velike količine glukoze**, posebno mozak.

Ako organizam nije izložen stalnim pikovima, njegov sustav može do duboke starosti održati relativno dobru sintezu inzulina u **gušterači**. Stalni pikovi, međutim, **iscrpljuju rezerve, odnosno same stanice**. Tada se, prije prelaska na sintetski inzulin, uzimaju **oralni antidijabetici**. Oni potiču preostale stanice da iskoriste sve rezerve. Među njima spominje stari **metformin**, za koji kaže da danas djeluje i kao protuupalni lijek.
sections.subtitle_en: Insulin lives for two minutes: how sweet bites exhaust the pancreas
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac reveals that the half-life of insulin in the blood is about two minutes
sections.content_en:
When asked which hormones are related to hunger and satiety, the guest announces a hormone that was hardly mentioned during her student days. Before that, she explains **insulin**. Insulin is a **peptide hormone**, built from amino acids like proteins, unlike steroid hormones. The difference is significant because peptide hormones in the blood are quickly broken down by protease enzymes.

She then asks the host a question: what is the half-life of insulin in the blood? He guesses around six hours. The answer surprises him: **about two minutes, or even less**. Hormones are chemical messengers that merely need to trigger a reaction. Insulin reacts immediately to the rise of glucose after a meal, that is, postprandially.

The guest then describes an everyday scenario. Someone eats a packaged cake in cellophane or a dry cookie with a sweet topping and drinks a can or carton of juice alongside it. Their glucose then rises very quickly. The boundaries within which glucose must remain in the blood are very narrow, roughly **from 3 to 5 millimoles per liter**. Anything above that is not good. But a drop below 3 is not harmless either, because without enough glucose a person can die. **The brain and heart consume large amounts of glucose**, especially the brain.

If the organism is not exposed to constant spikes, its system can maintain relatively good insulin synthesis in the **pancreas** into old age. Constant spikes, however, **exhaust the reserves, that is, the cells themselves**. Then, before switching to synthetic insulin, **oral antidiabetics** are taken. They stimulate the remaining cells to utilize all reserves. Among them, she mentions old **metformin**, which she says acts today as an anti-inflammatory drug as well.

sections.subtitle: Glukagon, rezerve u jetri i drevni instinkt lovca
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava ulogu glukagona i adrenalina u oslobađanju glukoze pri stresu
sections.content:
Drugi hormon gušterače je **glukagon**, za koji Donatella Verbanac kaže da djeluje suprotno inzulinu. Govoreći o njemu, objašnjava kako organizam gradi rezerve. Višak glukoze pohranjuje se ponajprije u **jetri**, gdje rezerve traju **barem 48 sati**, čak i bez unosa ugljikohidrata. Rezerve postoje i u **mišićima**, za mišićni rad.

Razlika je u tome kako se rezerve koriste. Kad je čovjek u stresu, **adrenalin i glukagon** potiču jetru da glukozu brzo otpusti u krv. U mišićima se glukoza otpušta u same mišićne stanice, dok je vrlo malo prelazi u krv. Tako čovjek može trčati, bilo za životinjom koju je spazio, bilo da bježi. Gošća to naziva **primordijalnim instinktom lovca**.

Na voditeljevo pitanje gošća potvrđuje da su glukagon i inzulin dva hormona usko vezana uz glad i sitost. Uloge im sažima ovako:
- **inzulin smanjuje glukozu u krvi** jer je unosi u stanice da se potroši,
- **glukagon izvlači pohranjene rezerve** i stavlja tu glukozu na raspolaganje.

To je, dodaje, „sve što smo znali do sad“. Danas se zna malo više, čime najavljuje razgovor o hormonu koji je promijenio razumijevanje sitosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Glucagon, reserves in the liver, and the ancient hunter's instinct
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the role of glucagon and adrenaline in releasing glucose under stress
sections.content_en:
The other hormone of the pancreas is **glucagon**, which Donatella Verbanac says acts opposite to insulin. Speaking of it, she explains how the organism builds reserves. Excess glucose is stored primarily in the **liver**, where reserves last **at least 48 hours**, even without carbohydrate intake. Reserves also exist in the **muscles**, for muscle work.

The difference lies in how reserves are used. When a person is under stress, **adrenaline and glucagon** stimulate the liver to quickly release glucose into the blood. In muscles, glucose is released into the muscle cells themselves, while very little of it passes into the blood. Thus a person can run, whether after an animal they spotted or to flee. The guest calls this the **primordial hunter's instinct**.

To the host's question, the guest confirms that glucagon and insulin are two hormones closely tied to hunger and satiety. She summarizes their roles like this:
- **insulin lowers glucose in the blood** because it brings it into cells to be consumed,
- **glucagon pulls out stored reserves** and makes that glucose available.

That is, she adds, "all that we knew until now." Today, a little more is known, thereby announcing the conversation about the hormone that changed the understanding of satiety.
