sections.subtitle: Leptin: hormon koji nastaje u masnim stanicama
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava tri razine masnog tkiva u ljudskom tijelu
sections.content:
Nakon razgovora o inzulinu i glukagonu, **Donatella Verbanac** uvodi hormon o kojem se, kako kaže, u njezino studentsko doba gotovo nije govorilo. Riječ je o **leptinu**, hormonu koji se sintetizira u masnim stanicama, odnosno u stanicama masnog tkiva. Inzulin i glukagon povezani su s osjećajem sitosti, no znanost danas zna više.

Da bi objasnila ulogu leptina, gošća najprije opisuje masno tkivo. Prema njezinim riječima, u tijelu postoje otprilike **tri razine masnog tkiva**:

- **potkožno masno tkivo**, koje čini otprilike trećinu,
- **visceralna masnoća**, odnosno mast oko unutarnjih organa,
- **masnoća koja određuje oblik tijela**.

Treću skupinu ilustrira primjerima. Neki ljudi imaju tanke noge, a punašniji su u gornjem dijelu tijela, osobito oko gornjeg dijela kukova, bokova i prsa. Drugi imaju oblik kruške: gornji dio tijela im je tanji, dok su noge i kukovi jači. Za taj se oblik, napominje gošća, kaže da je povoljniji.

## Masna stanica kao rezerva za najveću nuždu

Verbanac objašnjava da je masna stanica praktički sastavljena samo od masti. U njezinoj unutrašnjosti nalazi se vakuola puna masti, a ostale organele smještene su po rubu, između masne kapljice i stanične membrane. Masna stanica je zapravo **rezerva masti** i služi za najveću nuždu, u slučaju teške gladi. Tada tijelo mast crpi upravo iz masnog tkiva.

Da se skladištenje ne bi nastavljalo u nedogled, masne stanice sintetiziraju leptin. Taj hormon koristi slične puteve kao inzulin i djeluje na **hipotalamus**, odnosno na središnji živčani sustav. Gošća pritom naglašava da inzulin ne djeluje samo na periferna tkiva, nego i na središnja.

Leptin mozgu šalje poruku. U mozgu postoji svojevrsna vaga za sitost i glad, a leptin na nju javlja: „Stop, osjećaj gladi neka stane, ja sam sit.“ Kod osobe s normalnom količinom masnog tkiva taj sustav funkcionira jednostavno. Nakon obroka stvaraju se dodatne masnoće, one se uskladište i mozak dobiva signal da više ne treba jesti. Voditelj to sažima riječima da leptin hipotalamusu poručuje da je sve u redu. Gošća dodaje da tada tijelo ne treba sintetizirati hormone koji potiču glad, poput onih koji se danas pronalaze u crijevima.
sections.subtitle_en: Leptin: a hormone originating in fat cells
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains the three levels of adipose tissue in the human body
sections.content_en:
After the conversation about insulin and glucagon, **Donatella Verbanac** introduces a hormone about which, as she says, hardly anything was said in her student days. We are talking about **leptin**, a hormone synthesized in fat cells, that is, in cells of adipose tissue. Insulin and glucagon are connected to the feeling of satiety, but science knows more today.

To explain the role of leptin, the guest first describes adipose tissue. In her words, there are roughly **three levels of adipose tissue** in the body:

- **subcutaneous adipose tissue**, which makes up about a third,
- **visceral fat**, that is, fat around internal organs,
- **fat that determines body shape**.

She illustrates the third group with examples. Some people have thin legs and are plumper in the upper part of the body, especially around the upper hips, flanks, and chest. Others have a pear shape: their upper body is thinner, while their legs and hips are stronger. That shape, the guest notes, is said to be more favorable.

## The fat cell as a reserve for dire necessity

Verbanac explains that a fat cell is practically composed only of fat. In its interior is a vacuole full of fat, and other organelles are located along the edge, between the fat droplet and the cell membrane. The fat cell is actually a **fat reserve** and serves for dire necessity, in case of severe famine. Then the body draws fat precisely from adipose tissue.

So that storage does not continue indefinitely, fat cells synthesize leptin. That hormone uses pathways similar to insulin and acts on the **hypothalamus**, that is, on the central nervous system. In doing so, the guest emphasizes that insulin does not act only on peripheral tissues, but also on central ones.

Leptin sends a message to the brain. In the brain, there is a kind of scale for satiety and hunger, and leptin reports to it: "Stop, let the feeling of hunger cease, I am full." In a person with a normal amount of adipose tissue, that system functions simply. After a meal, additional fats are created, they are stored, and the brain receives a signal that it no longer needs to eat. The host summarizes this in the words that leptin conveys to the hypothalamus that everything is fine. The guest adds that then the body does not need to synthesize hormones that stimulate hunger, like those found in the intestines today.

sections.subtitle: Kad leptina ima previše, mozak ga prestaje „čuti“
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća uspoređuje receptore na stanicama s antenama i ključem koji ulazi u bravu
sections.content:
Problem nastaje kada masnog tkiva ima previše. Takvo stanje, podsjeća **Donatella Verbanac**, može biti posljedica neadekvatne prehrane u djetinjstvu ili epigenetskih promjena. Ako je majka bila pothranjena dok je dijete raslo u plodnoj vodi, dijete može dobiti poruku: „Meni je suđeno da svaku svoju kaloriju moram uskladištiti.“ Takvo će dijete, kako slikovito kaže, već do pete godine biti „fino popunjeno“.

Većoj količini masnog tkiva pripada i veća količina leptina. Masno tkivo ne prestaje lučiti taj hormon jer za to ne postoji nikakav signal. Gošća objašnjava i pojam **indeksa tjelesne mase**. Dobiva se tako da se tjelesna masa podijeli s kvadratom visine u metrima. Indeks se, prema njezinim riječima, općenito ne koristi previše, no kao kriterij za pretilost primjenjuje se granica od 30. Kod pretilih osoba krvlju kruži **tri do četiri puta više leptina** nego što je uobičajeno.

## Antene, ključevi i brave

Leptin je, kao i inzulin, peptidni hormon, ali je otporniji od mnogih drugih pa se zadržava u krvi u velikim količinama. Neravnoteža hormona s vremenom dovodi i do neravnoteže u **receptorima**. Gošća ih opisuje kao antene na površini stanica, primjerice stanica hipotalamusa. Uspoređuje ih s nekadašnjim „viklerima“ i dodaje da mlađe generacije, kako je primijetila kod studenata, više ne znaju što su vikleri. Voditelj se na to nasmije i kaže da ih se doslovno sjeća.

Gustoća receptora odgovara fiziološkoj koncentraciji hormona u serumu. Hormon i receptor pristaju jedan uz drugoga **kao ključ u bravu**. Kad se spoje, stanica dobiva poruku da ima dovoljno i da više ne treba jesti.

Ako hormona ima previše, stanica se brani od prepodraženosti. Dolazi do takozvane **rezistencije** ili **downregulacije receptora**: receptori se endocitozom povlače u unutrašnjost stanice. Gošća naglašava da je to normalna fiziološka regulacija. Posljedica je, međutim, da hormon više ne može djelovati, a mozak ne dobiva signal sitosti iako leptina u krvi ima u izobilju.
sections.subtitle_en: When there is too much leptin, the brain stops "hearing" it
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares receptors on cells to antennas and a key entering a lock
sections.content_en:
The problem arises when there is too much adipose tissue. Such a state, recalls **Donatella Verbanac**, can be the consequence of inadequate nutrition in childhood or epigenetic changes. If the mother was undernourished while the child was growing in amniotic fluid, the child may receive the message: "It is my destiny that I must store every single calorie of mine." Such a child, as she vividly says, will already be "nicely filled out" by age five.

A larger amount of adipose tissue also entails a larger amount of leptin. Adipose tissue does not stop secreting that hormone because no signal exists for that. The guest also explains the concept of **body mass index**. It is obtained by dividing body mass by the square of height in meters. The index, according to her words, is not overly used in general, but as a criterion for obesity a cutoff of 30 is applied. In obese people, **three to four times more leptin** circulates in the blood than is usual.

## Antennas, keys, and locks

Leptin is, like insulin, a peptide hormone, but it is more resistant than many others, so it lingers in the blood in large quantities. A hormonal imbalance over time also leads to an imbalance in **receptors**. The guest describes them as antennas on the surface of cells, for example cells of the hypothalamus. She compares them to old-fashioned "hair rollers" and adds that younger generations, as she noticed among students, no longer know what hair rollers are. The host laughs at that and says he literally remembers them.

The density of receptors corresponds to the physiological concentration of the hormone in serum. The hormone and receptor fit together **like a key in a lock**. When they connect, the cell receives the message that there is enough and that it no longer needs to eat.

If there is too much hormone, the cell defends itself against overstimulation. So-called **resistance** or **receptor downregulation** occurs: receptors retract into the interior of the cell via endocytosis. The guest emphasizes that this is normal physiological regulation. The consequence, however, is that the hormone can no longer act, and the brain does not receive the signal of satiety even though leptin abounds in the blood.

sections.subtitle: Hrana kao prijatelj i utjeha: zašto je osuđivanje pretilih nepravedno
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac govori o tome kako pretili ljudi nemaju osjećaj sitosti
sections.content:
Iz biokemijskog objašnjenja **Donatella Verbanac** izvodi zaključak s jasnom društvenom porukom. Okolina neprestano okrivljuje pretilog čovjeka, a on zapravo **ne može prestati jesti**. Hrana mu je potrebna fiziološki, psihološki i socijalno.

Za takve je ljude hrana, kaže gošća, veliki prijatelj, utjeha i drug, nešto u čemu se mogu veseliti. „I mi te ljude osuđujemo, a ti ljudi u biti nemaju osjećaj sitosti“, ističe. Zato, prema njezinim riječima, treba raditi na tome da se razina leptina u krvi smanji.

Time se zatvara krug koji je otvoren na početku razgovora. Tada je voditelj priznao da je i sam nekad pretile ljude osuđivao i smatrao da je sve pitanje discipline i volje.

## Začarani krug bez lakog izlaza

Voditelj sažima ono što je čuo. Velika količina masnog tkiva luči sve više leptina, a osoba više ne zna kako izaći iz tog stanja. Gošća potvrđuje da se radi o **začaranom krugu** i dodaje da je iz njega bez pomoći jako teško izaći.

Kao primjer navodi kirurške zahvate. Kad je ljudima uklonjeno suvišno visceralno masno tkivo, smanjila se količina masnog tkiva. Tada su u jednom trenutku ponovno počeli osjećati glad i sitost, upravo zato što se smanjila količina tkiva koje proizvodi leptin.
sections.subtitle_en: Food as a friend and comfort: why judging the obese is unfair
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac talks about how obese people do not have a feeling of satiety
sections.content_en:
From the biochemical explanation **Donatella Verbanac** draws a conclusion with a clear social message. Society constantly blames the obese person, yet they actually **cannot stop eating**. They need food physiologically, psychologically, and socially.

For such people food is, the guest says, a great friend, comfort, and companion, something in which they can rejoice. "And we judge those people, yet those people essentially have no feeling of satiety," she points out. Therefore, according to her words, one must work on reducing the level of leptin in the blood.

This closes the circle opened at the beginning of the conversation. Back then the host admitted that he himself once judged obese people and believed that everything was a matter of discipline and willpower.

## A vicious cycle with no easy exit

The host summarizes what he heard. A large amount of adipose tissue secretes more and more leptin, and the person no longer knows how to get out of that state. The guest confirms that this is a **vicious cycle** and adds that it is very hard to escape it without help.

As an example, she mentions surgical procedures. When people had excess visceral adipose tissue removed, the amount of adipose tissue decreased. Then at one point they began feeling hunger and satiety again, precisely because the amount of tissue producing leptin decreased.

sections.subtitle: GLP-1 lijekovi: agonisti koji pomažu prepoznati signal
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava što znači skraćenica GLP-1 i kako su otkriveni lijekovi za mršavljenje
sections.content:
Danas, nastavlja **Donatella Verbanac**, postoje lijekovi koji mijenjaju sliku liječenja pretilosti. Riječ je o takozvanim **inkretinskim lijekovima**. Gošća pojašnjava da ih ne bi nazvala hormonima. To su male molekule koje djeluju kao **agonisti**, a ne antagonisti, odnosno kao pomoćnici u prepoznavanju signala.

Na pitanje voditelja odgovara da skraćenica **GLP-1** znači *glucagon-like peptide-1*. Dodaje da postoje i kombinacije tih hormona. Ciljane molekule hormoni su koji se izlučuju u probavnom traktu ili ih izlučuje gušterača. Jedan od novih ciljeva koji se razvija jest **amilin**.

Riječ je o tvarima koje ranije nisu bile poznate. Do otkrića je došlo usput: lijekovi koji su djelovali kao agonisti tih receptora primjenjivali su se u liječenju **inzulinske rezistencije** i **šećerne bolesti tipa 2**, a liječnici su primijetili da ti pacijenti osjećaju manju glad.

## Povijest farmakoloških pokušaja

Budući da dosad nije postojalo dobro farmakološko rješenje za debljinu, gošća ne vidi ništa čudno u velikom „boomu“ ovih lijekova. Smatra da je on posve opravdan. Od 2000. godine pratila je dva ranija lijeka za mršavljenje:

- **Lijek sa središnjim djelovanjem** povučen je s tržišta negdje 2005. ili 2006. godine jer je štetno djelovao na srčani mišić.
- **Lijek s lokalnim djelovanjem**, koji je možda još negdje prisutan, uzimao se dvadesetak minuta prije jela. Vezao se na **lipazu**, enzim koji u probavnom sustavu razgrađuje masti, i sprječavao njezinu aktivaciju. Pojedena mast tako se izlučivala iz organizma.

Za drugi se lijek početkom 2000-ih tvrdilo da nije štetan jer se ne resorbira u krv. Izazivao je samo **steatoreju**, odnosno masnu stolicu, pa je osoba svakodnevno mogla vidjeti koliko je masti unijela. Ta mast nije ulazila u krv i zato je dolazilo do mršavljenja.

Gošća upozorava da se tada još nije dobro znalo kako takav pristup utječe na **mikrobiotu**. Kasnije se pokazalo da crijevo krcato neprobavljenom masti nije dobar okoliš za trilijune bakterija koje u njemu žive. Puno je bolje, zaključuje, te bakterije imati kao saveznike.
sections.subtitle_en: GLP-1 drugs: agonists that help recognize the signal
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains what the abbreviation GLP-1 means and how weight-loss drugs were discovered
sections.content_en:
Today, continues **Donatella Verbanac**, medications exist that are changing the landscape of obesity treatment. These are so-called **incretin drugs**. The guest clarifies that she would not call them hormones. These are small molecules that act as **agonists**, not antagonists, that is, as helpers in signal recognition.

To the host's question, she answers that the abbreviation **GLP-1** stands for *glucagon-like peptide-1*. She adds that combinations of these hormones also exist. The target molecules are hormones secreted in the digestive tract or secreted by the pancreas. One of the new targets being developed is **amylin**.

These are substances that were not previously known. The discovery happened along the way: drugs that acted as agonists of those receptors were used in the treatment of **insulin resistance** and **type 2 diabetes**, and physicians noticed that those patients felt less hunger.

## History of pharmacological attempts

Since no good pharmacological solution for obesity existed until now, the guest sees nothing strange in the great "boom" of these drugs. She considers it entirely justified. Since the year 2000, she tracked two earlier weight-loss drugs:

- **A centrally acting drug** was withdrawn from the market somewhere around 2005 or 2006 because it adversely affected heart muscle.
- **A locally acting drug**, which is perhaps still present somewhere, was taken about twenty minutes before a meal. It bound to **lipase**, an enzyme that breaks down fats in the digestive system, and prevented its activation. Eaten fat was thus excreted from the organism.

For the second drug, it was claimed in the early 2000s that it was not harmful because it is not resorbed into the blood. It caused only **steatorrhea**, that is, fatty stool, so a person could see daily how much fat they had ingested. That fat did not enter the blood and therefore weight loss occurred.

The guest warns that back then it was not yet well known how such an approach affected the **microbiota**. Later it turned out that an intestine crammed with undigested fat is not a good environment for the trillions of bacteria living in it. It is much better, she concludes, to have those bacteria as allies.

sections.subtitle: Reset začaranog kruga i mala studija na tri ispitanice
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj i gošća razgovaraju o tome kako GLP-1 lijekovi vraćaju osjetljivost na leptin
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što GLP-1 lijekovi zapravo rade s leptinom te smanjuju li ili povećavaju njegovu količinu. **Donatella Verbanac** objašnjava da ti lijekovi pomažu da se **signal ponovno uspostavi na pravi način**. Smanjuju inzulinsku rezistenciju pa organizam, a osobito hipotalamus, ponovno postaje osjetljiv i na inzulin i na leptin. Voditelj to opisuje kao reset začaranog kruga, a gošća se s tim slaže.

U razvoju su, dodaje, i kombinacije koje djeluju kao agonisti na dva ili tri hormona, što smatra vrlo obećavajućim. Za sebe kaže da je „jako veliki optimista“.

Spominje i diplomski rad koji je vodila zajedno s kolegom **Andrijom Karačićem**. U istraživanju su sudjelovale **tri žene** koje su se razlikovale po dobi, tjelesnoj masi i mikrobiomu. Istraživači su pratili kako na njih djeluje uzimanje takvog lijeka. Sve tri su se nakon toga jako dobro osjećale. Gošća ipak naglašava da je uzorak premalen da bi se iz njega bilo što generaliziralo.

Povjerenje u lijekove temelji na radu regulatornih tijela. Uvjerena je da ni američka **FDA**, ni europska **EMA**, ni hrvatski **HALMED** ne bi odobrili stavljanje lijeka u promet da nije provjeren. Za stručnjake HALMED-a kaže da su izvrsni. Nove generacije lijekova s drugim ciljnim molekulama, smatra, mogu napraviti još mnogo.

## Što jesti uz terapiju

Gošća podsjeća da uz lijekove postoji i prehrana. Profesorica **Darija Vranešić Bender** izradila je smjernice i vodič za prehranu osoba koje uzimaju takve lijekove. I u hrani se, prema riječima Verbanac, mogu pronaći molekule koje pomažu ukloniti suvišan leptin. Navodi **mlijeko i mliječne proizvode** te **suncokretove sjemenke**, koje opisuje kao odličnu „comfort food“.

Voditelj priznaje da voli grickalice, a gošća kaže da ih voli i ona. Umjesto industrijskih grickalica savjetuje:

- malo **oraha** i **badema**,
- **suncokretove** i **bučine sjemenke**,
- **kvalitetnu čokoladu**.

Takve grickalice, kaže, vraćaju dobro raspoloženje i istodobno osiguravaju kvalitetne namirnice.
sections.subtitle_en: Reset of the vicious cycle and a small study on three female subjects
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and guest discuss how GLP-1 drugs restore sensitivity to leptin
sections.content_en:
The host asks what GLP-1 drugs actually do with leptin and whether they reduce or increase its amount. **Donatella Verbanac** explains that these drugs help **re-establish the signal in the right way**. They reduce insulin resistance, so the organism, and especially the hypothalamus, becomes sensitive again to both insulin and leptin. The host describes this as a reset of the vicious cycle, and the guest agrees with that.

In development, she adds, are also combinations that act as agonists on two or three hormones, which she considers very promising. Of herself she says that she is "a very big optimist."

She also mentions a master's thesis she co-supervised with her colleague **Andrija Karačić**. Participating in the study were **three women** who differed in age, body mass, and microbiome. The researchers tracked how taking such a drug affected them. All three felt very good afterward. The guest nevertheless emphasizes that the sample is too small to generalize anything from it.

She bases her trust in medications on the work of regulatory bodies. She is convinced that neither the American **FDA**, nor the European **EMA**, nor the Croatian **HALMED** would approve placing a drug on the market if it had not been verified. Of HALMED experts, she says they are excellent. New generations of drugs with other target molecules, she believes, can achieve much more.

## What to eat alongside therapy

The guest reminds that alongside drugs there is also nutrition. Professor **Darija Vranešić Bender** developed nutritional guidelines and a guide for people taking such medications. In food too, according to Verbanac, molecules can be found that help clear excess leptin. She cites **milk and dairy products** and **sunflower seeds**, which she describes as great "comfort food."

The host admits that he loves snacks, and the guest says that she loves them too. Instead of industrial snacks, she advises:

- a few **walnuts** and **almonds**,
- **sunflower** and **pumpkin seeds**,
- **high-quality chocolate**.

Such snacks, she says, restore a good mood and simultaneously provide quality ingredients.

sections.subtitle: Od ćelavosti do erektilne disfunkcije: lijekovi koji su pronašli novu namjenu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj se šali pitajući kada će izmisliti lijek za ćelavost
sections.content:
U opuštenijem dijelu razgovora voditelj, kako sam kaže, „malo sebično“ pita kada će netko smisliti lijek za ćelavost. Pomaci kod debljine zahvaljujući GLP-1 lijekovima, šali se, već su postignuti. **Donatella Verbanac** odgovara da se na tome radi. Podsjeća da se djelatna tvar **minoksidil** dugo koristila za liječenje povišenoga krvnog tlaka.

Voditelj uočava obrazac: GLP-1 lijekovi bili su usmjereni na dijabetes, a minoksidil na krvni tlak. Lijekovi, primjećuje, često pomognu i kod nečega što uopće nije bila njihova prvotna namjena.

Gošća dodaje najpoznatiji primjer, **lijek za erektilnu disfunkciju**. Izvorno je razvijen za plućnu arterijsku hipertenziju, ali u tome nije bio posve učinkovit niti je za tu dijagnozu bio prihvaćen. Ljudi, osobito muškarci, ipak ga nisu htjeli prestati uzimati. Tako je nastala nova indikacija, koja je donijela golemu zaradu kompaniji proizvođaču, a kasnije i generičkim tvrtkama.

## „Old school“ disciplina koja traje desetljećima

Voditelj zatim iznosi osobno iskustvo. U svom krugu ima nekoliko pretilih osoba. Kad im je predložio da isprobaju te lijekove, odbili su: žele to riješiti „old school“, disciplinom i voljom. Problem, međutim, kod njih traje već 10, 15 ili 20 godina.

Gošća odgovara da svako odugovlačenje, prema njezinu mišljenju, šteti i da je potrebno shvatiti ozbiljnost stanja. Iz toga prelazi na temu povjerenja u farmaceutsku industriju.
sections.subtitle_en: From baldness to erectile dysfunction: drugs that found a new purpose
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host jokes, asking when they will invent a cure for baldness
sections.content_en:
In a more relaxed part of the conversation, the host, as he says himself, "a bit selfishly" asks when someone will come up with a cure for baldness. Progress with obesity thanks to GLP-1 drugs, he jokes, has already been achieved. **Donatella Verbanac** replies that this is being worked on. She recalls that the active substance **minoxidil** was used for a long time to treat high blood pressure.

The host notices a pattern: GLP-1 drugs were targeted at diabetes, and minoxidil at blood pressure. Medications, he observes, often help with something that was not their original purpose at all.

The guest adds the most famous example, a **drug for erectile dysfunction**. It was originally developed for pulmonary arterial hypertension, but was not entirely effective in that, nor was it approved for that diagnosis. People, especially men, nevertheless did not want to stop taking it. Thus a new indication arose, which brought enormous earnings to the manufacturing company, and later to generic companies.

## "Old school" discipline lasting decades

The host then shares a personal experience. He has several obese people in his circle. When he suggested they try these drugs, they refused: they want to solve it "old school," through discipline and willpower. The problem, however, has been going on for 10, 15, or 20 years for them.

The guest replies that any stalling, in her opinion, causes harm and that it is necessary to realize the seriousness of the condition. From there she moves to the topic of trust in the pharmaceutical industry.

sections.subtitle: Farmaceutska industrija: zlikovac ili spasiteljica?
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća s oduševljenjem govori o otkriću inzulina 1922. i hrvatskom Sumamedu
sections.content:
**Donatella Verbanac** govori iz iskustva. Deset godina radila je u istraživanju i razvoju lijekova, u Plivinu istraživačkom institutu i u multinacionalnoj farmaceutskoj kompaniji, na pretkliničkim i kliničkim istraživanjima. Na čestu primjedbu da su lijekovi skupi odgovara da je svaki dan rada jednog istraživača, od potrošenih kemikalija nadalje, iznimno skup. Ističe i da su klinička istraživanja vrlo rigorozna. Kad multicentrične studije faze 3 na tisućama ljudi pokažu pozitivne rezultate i kad se lijek koristi prema uputama, opasnosti nema, iako svaki lijek ima neku nuspojavu.

Voditelj podsjeća da je u vrijeme Covida, uz medijsku pompu, lažne vijesti i snažne stavove za i protiv, bilo teško ostati objektivan. Tada je, smatra, farmaceutska industrija bila demonizirana i dobila status zlikovca. Otkriva i zanimljivost iz svoje prošlosti: završio je farmaceutsku srednju školu. Profesorice su ga tijekom ljetne prakse pripremale za fakultet, ali on im je odmah rekao da neće upisati farmaciju. Na kraju je završio ekonomiju.

## Inzulin, penicilin i Sumamed

Gošća podsjeća na dobrobiti koje je industrija donijela:

- **Inzulin** se na tržištu pojavio **1922. godine**. Do tada je dijabetes tipa 1 bio smrtonosna bolest, a djeca su umirala oko 12. ili 13. godine, kad su rast i razvoj najintenzivniji. Kada su znanstvenici pročistili ekstrakt pseće gušterače i primijenili ga, bilo je to, kaže gošća, kao da su djecu „uskrsnuli“. Počela su rasti, jesti i uživati u životu.
- **Penicilin** je spasio ljude od sepse i bakterijskih bolesti koje su do tada bile smrtonosne.
- **Azitromicin**, odnosno **Sumamed**, razvijen je u Zagrebu, u **Plivi**. Licencu je kasnije preuzeo **Pfizer**, koji je za cijelo vrijeme trajanja licence 10 posto neto dobiti davao Plivi. Prema riječima gošće, i danas nema boljeg antibiotika. Pliviny znanstvenike naziva fenomenalnima i kaže da su spasili tisuće ljudi i djece. Za odrasle navodi dozu od 500 miligrama tijekom tri dana, a za djecu tri puta po 250 miligrama.

Higijena je, kaže, pola zdravlja, a drugu polovicu čini poštena, fer i etična znanost u farmaceutskoj industriji.

## Svaki dan na tržištu vrijedi milijune

Gošća objašnjava razliku između akademije i industrije. Akademiji je primarna funkcija edukacija, a istraživanje je sekundarno. U farmaceutskoj industriji sve je podređeno tome da se do uspješnog pokusa dođe što brže. Čim stigne negativan rezultat, odmah postoji rezervni plan. Razlog je jednostavan: svaki dan na tržištu je važan. Ako lijek godišnje donosi 2,5 milijarde dolara prodaje, dovoljno je taj iznos podijeliti s 365 dana pa da se vidi koliko milijuna dolara vrijedi svaki izgubljeni dan.
sections.subtitle_en: The pharmaceutical industry: villain or savior?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks enthusiastically about the discovery of insulin in 1922 and Croatian Sumamed
sections.content_en:
**Donatella Verbanac** speaks from experience. For ten years she worked in drug research and development, at Pliva's research institute and in a multinational pharmaceutical company, on preclinical and clinical research. To the frequent remark that medications are expensive, she replies that each day of a researcher's work, from consumed chemicals onward, is extremely expensive. She also emphasizes that clinical trials are very rigorous. When phase 3 multicenter studies on thousands of people show positive results and when a drug is used according to instructions, there is no danger, although every medication has some side effect.

The host recalls that during Covid, alongside media hype, fake news, and strong opinions for and against, it was hard to remain objective. Back then, he believes, the pharmaceutical industry was demonized and gained the status of a villain. He also reveals an interesting detail from his past: he graduated from a pharmaceutical secondary school. The professors prepared him for university during summer internship, but he immediately told them he would not enroll in pharmacy. In the end, he graduated in economics.

## Insulin, penicillin, and Sumamed

The guest recalls the benefits the industry has brought:

- **Insulin** appeared on the market in **1922**. Until then, type 1 diabetes was a fatal disease, and children died around age 12 or 13, when growth and development are most intensive. When scientists purified canine pancreas extract and applied it, it was, the guest says, as if they had "resurrected" the children. They began to grow, eat, and enjoy life.
- **Penicillin** saved people from sepsis and bacterial diseases that were fatal until then.
- **Azithromycin**, that is **Sumamed**, was developed in Zagreb, at **Pliva**. The license was later taken over by **Pfizer**, which gave 10 percent of net profit to Pliva for the entire duration of the license. In the guest's words, there is still no better antibiotic today. She calls Pliva's scientists phenomenal and says they saved thousands of people and children. For adults, she states a dose of 500 milligrams over three days, and for children three times 250 milligrams.

Hygiene, she says, is half of health, and the other half consists of honest, fair, and ethical science in the pharmaceutical industry.

## Every day on the market is worth millions

The guest explains the difference between academia and industry. Academia's primary function is education, while research is secondary. In the pharmaceutical industry, everything is subordinated to reaching a successful experiment as quickly as possible. As soon as a negative result arrives, a backup plan exists immediately. The reason is simple: every day on the market is important. If a drug brings 2.5 billion dollars in sales annually, it is enough to divide that amount by 365 days to see how many millions of dollars each lost day is worth.

sections.subtitle: Pretilost kao kronična bolest i strah od doživotne terapije
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava zašto pretilost treba liječiti kao kroničnu bolest
sections.content:
**Donatella Verbanac** smatra da razumije zašto su ljudi sumnjičavi prema GLP-1 lijekovima. Ti se lijekovi još ne izdaju svima na recept pa ih vjerojatno treba plaćati. Ljudi se pitaju i hoće li im se kilogrami, odnosno apetit, vratiti kad prestanu uzimati lijek. Gošća odgovara: vjerojatno da.

Zato poručuje da **pretilost treba početi tretirati kao bolest**. To stanje, kaže, uzrokuje stotinu različitih bolesti u organizmu: od upale niskog stupnja i disbioze do psihičkih bolesti i oštećenja zglobova, poput artritisa. Ipak se, prema njezinim riječima, ne shvaća dovoljno ozbiljno. Ljudi razmišljaju: „Skupo je, nudi mi se, tko zna vrijedi li.“ Gošća smatra da terapiju treba prihvatiti objeručke i slijediti savjete dobro educiranih liječnika. Mnogi od njih gostovali su u ovom podcastu, a ona ih opisuje kao moralne ljude koji stoje iza svojih rezultata.

Uspoređuje to s **lijekovima za povišeni krvni tlak**. Nitko ne bi smio razmišljati: „Kad mi se tlak malo smanji, prestat ću.“ U tom slučaju tlak će ponovno porasti.

## Odbojnost prema riječi „doživotno“

Voditelj priznaje da je upravo to ljudima najveća muka. Ne vole biti na kroničnoj terapiji, a misao da će neki lijek morati uzimati do kraja života, kaže, muči i njega osobno.

Gošća podsjeća da su ljudi isto tako bili nesklono raspoloženi prema **lijekovima za visok kolesterol**. Takvo stanje ponekad je posljedica obiteljske hiperkolesterolemije, osobito kad osoba uđe u treću životnu dob ili postane manje tjelesno aktivna. Novi radovi, navodi, pokazuju da su lijekovi koji inhibiraju sintezu kolesterola pomogli spriječiti bolesti koje su dobivali ljudi koji te lijekove nisu uzimali.

Minimalne doze uzimaju se jednom dnevno, prema uputama. Gošća najavljuje da će i GLP agonisti uskoro postojati u **oralnom obliku**, a ne samo kao injekcije. Na kraju postavlja retoričko pitanje: kako se nadamo doživjeti određenu životnu dob ako ne koristimo ono što nam stoji na raspolaganju?
sections.subtitle_en: Obesity as a chronic disease and the fear of lifelong therapy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains why obesity should be treated as a chronic disease
sections.content_en:
**Donatella Verbanac** believes she understands why people are suspicious of GLP-1 drugs. These drugs are not yet prescribed to everyone on prescription, so people probably have to pay for them. People also wonder whether their kilograms, or rather appetite, will return once they stop taking the medication. The guest replies: probably yes.

That is why she says that **we must begin treating obesity as a disease**. That condition, she says, causes a hundred different diseases in the body: from low-grade inflammation and dysbiosis to mental illnesses and joint damage, like arthritis. Yet, according to her words, it is not taken seriously enough. People think: "It's expensive, it's being offered to me, who knows if it's worth it." The guest believes therapy should be welcomed with open arms and the advice of well-educated physicians followed. Many of them have been guests on this podcast, and she describes them as moral people who stand behind their results.

She compares this to **medications for high blood pressure**. No one should think: "When my blood pressure drops a bit, I'll stop." In that case, blood pressure will rise again.

## Aversion to the word "lifelong"

The host admits that this is precisely people's greatest torment. They do not like being on chronic therapy, and the thought that they will have to take some medication until the end of life, he says, torments him personally as well.

The guest recalls that people were likewise disinclined toward **medications for high cholesterol**. Such a condition is sometimes the result of familial hypercholesterolemia, especially when a person enters the third age of life or becomes less physically active. New papers, she states, show that drugs that inhibit cholesterol synthesis helped prevent diseases contracted by people who did not take those drugs.

Minimal doses are taken once a day, according to instructions. The guest announces that GLP agonists will soon also exist in **oral form**, not just as injections. In the end, she poses a rhetorical question: how do we hope to reach a certain age if we do not use what is at our disposal?

sections.subtitle: Je li moguća trajna promjena bez lijekova?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita postoji li put do trajne promjene uz kratkotrajnu primjenu lijekova
sections.content:
Voditelj otvara temu dugovječnosti. Govori o prijateljima koji su pretili, a „super inteligentni“ su ljudi. Dugo je mislio da je uzrok njihove pretilosti emotivne ili psihološke prirode, možda neka „emotivna štaka“ koja je bila početni okidač. Sada, nakon objašnjenja o hormonalnom disbalansu, smatra da je ljudima u četrdesetima, kako kaže ne želeći nikoga plašiti, doslovno vrijeme da nešto poduzmu. Prisjeća se i šifre dijagnoze debljine koju je gošća spomenula, a ona ga upućuje da je provjeri jer ni sama nije sigurna u točnu oznaku.

Zatim postavlja ključno pitanje. Ako se lijekovi uzmu akutno, kao privremena pomoć, postoji velika šansa da se ljudi vrate starim obrascima i kilogramima. Ima li gošća, kao netko tko se cijeli život bavi hranom i biokemijom, put do **trajne promjene bez kontinuiranog uzimanja lijekova**?

## „Nije moja zadaća liječiti“

**Donatella Verbanac** odgovara oprezno. Čim postoji dijagnoza, riječ je o bolesti. I sama poznaje ljude koji su uzimali ili još uzimaju te lijekove. Naglašava, međutim, da se ne želi miješati u nešto što nije njezina struka jer njezina zadaća nije postavljati dijagnoze ni liječiti. Predlaže da se o tome razgovara s endokrinologom. On bi, kaže, mogao objasniti da se problem trenutačno ne može brzo riješiti bez istraživanja i dokaza o tome kako bi neka druga intervencija mogla dugoročno ići usporedno s terapijom.

Lijekovi su na tržištu tek nedavno, a praćenje korisnika u eksperimentalnim uvjetima traje najviše pet do šest godina. Najbolje studije objavljene u časopisu ***New England Journal of Medicine*** pokazuju, prema njezinim riječima, da ih treba koristiti dugoročno. Za sada je to **kronična terapija**.

## Vježbanje samo nije dovoljno

Gošća dodaje još jednu stvar koju zna sa sigurnošću. Ako netko želi smršavjeti samo vježbanjem, u teretani ili dvorani, potrošene kalorije gotovo su zanemarive u odnosu na ono što unese jednim dobrim sendvičem. To slikovito opisuje kao „nulu“. Priznaje da ni sama ponekad ne može odoljeti mirisu određenih narezaka jer imaju savršeno izbalansiranu slanost, slatkoću i miris, koji bude apetit.
sections.subtitle_en: Is permanent change possible without medication?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks if there is a path to permanent change with short-term drug use
sections.content_en:
The host opens the topic of longevity. He speaks of friends who are obese, yet are "super intelligent" people. For a long time, he thought that the cause of their obesity was emotional or psychological in nature, perhaps some "emotional crutch" that was the initial trigger. Now, after the explanation about hormonal imbalance, he believes that for people in their forties, as he says not wanting to scare anyone, it is literally time to take action. He also recalls the obesity diagnosis code mentioned by the guest, and she directs him to check it because she is not certain of the exact designation herself.

Then he poses a key question. If drugs are taken acutely, as temporary help, a strong chance exists that people will return to old patterns and kilograms. Does the guest, as someone who has dealt with food and biochemistry all her life, have a path to **permanent change without continuous drug intake**?

## "It is not my task to treat"

**Donatella Verbanac** answers cautiously. As soon as a diagnosis exists, it is a matter of disease. She herself knows people who took or are still taking these drugs. She emphasizes, however, that she does not want to interfere in something that is not her profession because her task is neither making diagnoses nor treating. She suggests discussing this with an endocrinologist. He could, she says, explain that the problem cannot currently be resolved quickly without research and evidence on how some other intervention could go hand in hand with therapy over the long term.

The drugs have been on the market only recently, and monitoring users in experimental conditions lasts at most five to six years. The best studies published in the ***New England Journal of Medicine*** show, according to her words, that they need to be used long-term. For now, it is **chronic therapy**.

## Exercise alone is not enough

The guest adds one more thing she knows with certainty. If someone wants to lose weight through exercise alone, in the gym or sports hall, the calories burned are almost negligible compared to what is ingested with a single good sandwich. She vividly describes this as "zero." She admits that she herself sometimes cannot resist the smell of certain cold cuts because they have a perfectly balanced saltiness, sweetness, and aroma that awaken the appetite.

sections.subtitle: Prehrambena industrija i pitanje integriteta
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj se pita zašto se prehrambena industrija demonizira manje od farmaceutske
sections.content:
Od narezaka **Donatella Verbanac** prelazi na širu sliku. Kao što farmaceutska industrija razvija lijekove, tako i **prehrambena industrija** vrlo dobro zna kako privući kupce. Ima optimalnu količinu masti da proizvod bude slastan, jer „bez masti nije dobro“, te dovoljno soli i šećera da se svidi.

Voditelj primjećuje da se prehrambena industrija demonizira znatno manje od farmaceutske. Gošća se slaže, ali ne želi ništa reći protiv nje. Voditelj dodaje da nikoga ne treba demonizirati jer su svi ljudi, a gošća zaključuje da svatko nastoji osigurati egzistenciju.

## Od malog poduzetnika do korporacije

Voditelj razvija misao. Netko krene kao mali poduzetnik i bori se da njegov proizvod uspije kako bi osigurao život svojoj obitelji. Prođe 10, 20, 30 ili 40 godina, tvrtka postane uspješna, a on je cijelo vrijeme razmišljao kako da proizvod bolje prodaje. Pitanje je, kaže, što tada ostaje od integriteta: donose li se moralne i etičke odluke ili je **profit jedino mjerilo**?

Gošća kao primjer navodi kompanije koje su na tržištu već oko 150 godina, s napicima koji su i danas najpopularniji i čije se reklame mogu vidjeti posvuda. Voditelj dodaje i snagu marketinga.

Gošća ipak ističe i drugu stranu. Te kompanije imaju logistiku kojom dopiru do najudaljenijih dijelova svijeta, a njihovi se transportni sustavi koriste i u dobre svrhe. U njihovim hladnjačama, kaže, lijekovi stižu tamo gdje su potrebni, a dvadesetak posto kapaciteta može se posvetiti takvim namjenama.

Ne treba demonizirati svaku stvar, zaključuje. Ključna je **edukacija**, i to od najranije dobi, o tome koliko se može postići svakodnevnim navikama. Hranjenje je primordijalna ljudska potreba, a pravilno hranjenje najbolji je zalog zdravog metabolizma u kasnijem životu.
sections.subtitle_en: The food industry and the question of integrity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host wonders why the food industry is demonized less than the pharmaceutical industry
sections.content_en:
From cold cuts **Donatella Verbanac** moves to the broader picture. Just as the pharmaceutical industry develops drugs, so the **food industry** knows very well how to attract customers. It has the optimal amount of fat to make the product delicious, because "without fat it's not good," and enough salt and sugar to be pleasing.

The host observes that the food industry is demonized considerably less than the pharmaceutical one. The guest agrees, but does not want to say anything against it. The host adds that no one should be demonized because all are human, and the guest concludes that everyone strives to secure a livelihood.

## From small entrepreneur to corporation

The host develops the thought. Someone starts as a small entrepreneur and fights for their product to succeed in order to secure a living for their family. 10, 20, 30, or 40 years pass, the company becomes successful, and all that time he thought about how to sell the product better. The question, he says, is what remains of integrity then: are moral and ethical decisions made, or is **profit the sole metric**?

As an example, the guest cites companies that have been on the market for about 150 years, with beverages that are still the most popular today and whose advertisements can be seen everywhere. The host adds the power of marketing as well.

The guest nevertheless highlights the other side as well. Those companies have the logistics to reach the most remote parts of the world, and their transport systems are used for good purposes too. In their refrigerated trucks, she says, medicines reach where they are needed, and about twenty percent of capacity can be dedicated to such purposes.

One should not demonize everything, she concludes. Key is **education**, from the earliest age, about how much can be achieved through daily habits. Feeding is a primordial human need, and proper feeding is the best pledge of healthy metabolism in later life.

sections.subtitle: Stanica, hrana i kisik: gdje počinje začarani krug
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava da su hrana i kisik temelj rada svake stanice
sections.content:
Voditelj se vraća na začarani krug leptina, inzulina i glukoze te pita **što je njegov ulaz**. Predlaže da se epigenetsko i genetsko nasljeđe baka, djedova i roditelja, na koje više ne možemo utjecati, za trenutak zanemari. Zanima ga ono za što pojedinac može preuzeti odgovornost. Je li početak svega hrana?

**Donatella Verbanac** predlaže da se krene od **pojedinačne stanice**, onakve kakvu smo naslijedili rođenjem. Neke stvari ne možemo mijenjati, poput određenih genetskih bolesti koje su, kako kaže, kao sudbina usađene u stanicu. Ipak, zahvaljuje Bogu što danas postoji mogućnost da se i one riješe. Podsjeća i na ranije spomenute epigenetske promjene.

## Dva temelja metabolizma

Osnovno što pokreće stanicu, objašnjava gošća, jesu **tvar i kisik**: hrana koju jedemo i kisik koji udišemo. Zato je važno naučiti se pravilno hraniti, ali i znati kako treba disati. To osigurava normalan metabolizam i razgradnju hrane do ugljičnog dioksida i vode.

Iz tog procesa dobivamo **toplinsku energiju**, kojom održavamo tjelesnu temperaturu, i **kemijsku energiju** za rad. Na kraju dodaje da sigurno postoje i neke druge vrste energije za koje još ne znamo.
sections.subtitle_en: Cell, food, and oxygen: where the vicious cycle begins
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that food and oxygen are the foundation of every cell's work
sections.content_en:
The host returns to the vicious cycle of leptin, insulin, and glucose and asks **what its entry point is**. He proposes setting aside for a moment the epigenetic and genetic inheritance of grandmothers, grandfathers, and parents, which we can no longer influence. He is interested in what an individual can take responsibility for. Is food the beginning of everything?

**Donatella Verbanac** proposes starting from the **individual cell**, the kind we inherited at birth. Some things we cannot change, like certain genetic diseases that are, as she says, implanted in the cell like destiny. Still, she thanks God that today the possibility exists to resolve them as well. She also recalls the previously mentioned epigenetic changes.

## Two pillars of metabolism

The basic thing that drives the cell, the guest explains, is **substance and oxygen**: the food we eat and the oxygen we breathe. Therefore, it is important to learn to eat properly, but also to know how to breathe. That ensures normal metabolism and the breakdown of food into carbon dioxide and water.

From that process we get **thermal energy**, by which we maintain body temperature, and **chemical energy** for work. In the end she adds that there are certainly other types of energy as well of which we are not yet aware.
