sections.subtitle: Zamka ultraprocesirane hrane: brže pojedeno, pola više u tanjuru
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava zašto se procesirana hrana jede brže i u većim količinama
sections.content:
Voditelj se vraća na podatak s početka razgovora o prosječnoj velikoj trgovini s čak **300.000 različitih artikala**. Pita ima li ikakve dobrobiti za ljude koji se svakodnevno hrane kupovnom hranom iz trgovačkih centara ili zbog užurbanog načina života često naručuju jela iz restorana. Zanima ga to čak i u slučajevima kada je tjelesna težina pod kontrolom, uz otvoreno pitanje visceralne masti.

**Donatella Verbanac** odgovara konkretnim podatkom. Procesirane hrane, kaže, pojede se **otprilike 50 posto više** nego obične, neprocesirane. Razlog je jednostavan: takva se hrana jede brže. Na voditeljevo pitanje zašto je tako, objašnjava da je procesirana hrana već djelomično pripremljena i razgrađena. To mogu biti praškovi ili razni dodaci koji se ubacuju u proizvod.

Kao primjer navodi pire krumpir u prahu. Takav pire, za razliku od kuhanog krumpira, pojede se **dvaput brže**, a pojede ga se i 50 posto više. Poruka je jasna: tijelo procesiranu hranu prima brže nego što stigne registrirati sitost. Na to se nadovezuje ono što je gošća objasnila ranije u razgovoru, da se osjećaj sitosti javlja tek dvadesetak minuta nakon jela.
sections.subtitle_en: The trap of ultra-processed food: eaten faster, half more on the plate
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains why processed food is eaten faster and in larger quantities
sections.content_en:
The host returns to the data from the beginning of the conversation about an average large grocery store with as many as **300,000 different items**. He asks whether there is any benefit for people who feed themselves daily on store-bought food from shopping centers or, due to a hectic lifestyle, frequently order meals from restaurants. He is interested in this even in cases when body weight is under control, with the open question of visceral fat.

**Donatella Verbanac** answers with concrete data. Processed food, she says, is eaten **roughly 50 percent more** than ordinary, unprocessed food. The reason is simple: such food is eaten faster. To the host's question why this is so, she explains that processed food is already partially prepared and broken down. These can be powders or various additives put into the product.

As an example, she mentions instant mashed potatoes. Such puree, unlike boiled potatoes, is eaten **twice as fast**, and 50 percent more of it is eaten. The message is clear: the body receives processed food faster than it manages to register satiety. This ties in with what the guest explained earlier in the conversation, that the feeling of satiety occurs only about twenty minutes after eating.

sections.subtitle: Bakina juha u prahu i obroci za američku vojsku
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava liofilizaciju i priču o vojnim obrocima Ancela Keysa
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim pita za postupak **liofilizacije**. Donatella Verbanac ga opisuje kao uobičajen fizikalno-kemijski postupak: namirnica, na primjer bjelančevina, zamrzne se, a zatim se pod posebnim uvjetima tlaka iz nje otkloni praktički sva voda. Ostaje suha tvar. Napominje da postupak traje jako dugo.

Voditelj potom postavlja slikovito pitanje. Ako bi njegova baka skuhala juhu i ta se juha liofilizacijom pretvorila u prah, bi li to bila procesirana hrana? Gošća odgovara da bi **dijelom** bila, jer je primijenjen postupak obrade. No ako je baka u juhu stavila sve što treba, a uklonjena je samo voda, u prahu bi ostali svi mikropeptidi, proteini i ostali vrijedni sastojci. Vodu bi trebalo samo nadoknaditi.

Pitanje je gošću podsjetilo na vojne obroke. Voditelj priznaje da je vojni rok "taman izbjegao", a ona se prisjeća obroka označenih slovom K koji su nastali u američkoj vojsci. Navodi da je na njima, prema pričama, radio i **Ancel Keys**, kojeg naziva ocem mediteranske prehrane i autorom najveće studije provedene na Mediteranu.

Riječ je o suhim, dehidriranim ili liofiliziranim komadima pakiranima u konzerve ili nepropusne vrećice. Njihov sastav bio je pažljivo uravnotežen:

- **50 do 60 posto** ugljikohidrata
- **oko 30 posto** masti
- ostatak bjelančevine

Takav obrok pokriva fiziološke potrebe u jednom obroku. Gošća ga uspoređuje s današnjim varivom od mahunarki uz dodatak mesa, piletine ili jajeta. Dodaje da su ovakvi obroci dragocjeni i izvan rata, u slučaju bilo kakvih nepogoda, te da sigurno postoje u državnim rezervama. Zaključuje da je liofilizacija postupak **bez previše utjecaja kemije**: uklanjanjem vode stvaraju se uvjeti u kojima ne mogu rasti plijesni i bakterije, pa nastaje dobar, sterilan, suh proizvod.
sections.subtitle_en: Grandmother's powdered soup and meals for the US Army
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains freeze-drying and the story of Ancel Keys' military rations
sections.content_en:
The host then asks about the process of **lyophilization**. Donatella Verbanac describes it as a standard physicochemical procedure: a food item, for example protein, is frozen, and then under special pressure conditions practically all water is removed from it. Dry matter remains. She notes that the procedure takes a very long time.

The host then poses a vivid question. If his grandmother cooked soup and that soup was turned into powder by lyophilization, would that be processed food? The guest answers that it would **partially** be, because a processing procedure was applied. But if grandma put everything needed into the soup, and only water was removed, all micropeptides, proteins, and other valuable ingredients would remain in the powder. One would only need to replenish the water.

The question reminded the guest of military rations. The host admits that he "just barely avoided" military service, and she recalls rations marked with the letter K that originated in the US Army. She states that, according to stories, **Ancel Keys**, whom she calls the father of the Mediterranean diet and author of the largest study conducted in the Mediterranean, also worked on them.

These were dry, dehydrated, or lyophilized portions packed in cans or impermeable pouches. Their composition was carefully balanced:

- **50 to 60 percent** carbohydrates
- **about 30 percent** fats
- the remainder proteins

Such a meal covers physiological needs in a single meal. The guest compares it to today's legume stew with added meat, chicken, or an egg. She adds that such meals are precious outside of war as well, in case of any disasters, and that they certainly exist in state reserves. She concludes that lyophilization is a procedure **without excessive chemical influence**: by removing water, conditions are created in which mold and bacteria cannot grow, yielding a good, sterile, dry product.

sections.subtitle: Etiketa otkriva istinu: što više sastojaka, to više procesiranja
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac opisuje kako čita deklaracije na pakiranjima hrane
sections.content:
Voditelj pita nije li i neprocesirana hrana danas lošije kvalitete nego prije pedeset godina. Donatella Verbanac priznaje da vjerojatno jest, jer se navodno i tlo jako promijenilo. Ipak, ističe da nije sklona sve gledati negativno. Duboko vjeruje u ono što se uzgaja i smatra da je hrana koju se može nabaviti u Hrvatskoj **još uvijek izuzetno dobre kvalitete**.

Zatim otkriva kako sama procjenjuje koliko je neki proizvod procesiran. Prvo čita etikete. Na sumnju je navode natpisi poput "bez glutena", "bez soli", "bez šećera" ili "bez masti", nakon kojih s druge strane pakiranja otkrije dugačak popis sastojaka.

Posebno se osvrće na **trend proteina**, koji naziva aktualnim hitom i hypeom. Svi danas žele što više proteina kroz namirnice. Gošća postavlja tri pitanja koja bi trebalo imati na umu:

- što je dodano da bi proteina bilo više,
- koliko ih zaista ima više,
- koliko ih tijelo zapravo može iskoristiti.

Njezino pravilo je jednostavno: **sve što ima puno sastojaka, za nju je procesirano.**
sections.subtitle_en: The label reveals the truth: the more ingredients, the more processing
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac describes how she reads declarations on food packaging
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether unprocessed food today is not also of poorer quality than fifty years ago. Donatella Verbanac admits that it probably is, because the soil has supposedly changed a lot too. Still, she emphasizes that she is not inclined to look at everything negatively. She deeply believes in what is grown and considers the food that can be obtained in Croatia to be **still of exceptionally good quality**.

Then she reveals how she herself assesses how processed a product is. First she reads the labels. Phrases such as "gluten-free," "salt-free," "sugar-free," or "fat-free" arouse suspicion in her, after which she discovers a long list of ingredients on the other side of the packaging.

She particularly touches upon the **protein trend**, which she calls the current hit and hype. Everyone today wants as much protein as possible through groceries. The guest poses three questions that should be kept in mind:

- what was added so there would be more protein,
- how much more is there really,
- how much of it can the body actually utilize.

Her rule is simple: **anything with a lot of ingredients is processed to her.**

sections.subtitle: Lekcija hrvatskog maslinovog ulja: od masline u moru do vrhunskih nagrada
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća prepričava kako su maslinari nekad odgorčavali masline u moru
sections.content:
Na pitanje podcjenjuju li ljudi važnost prehrane za zdravlje, Donatella Verbanac odgovara optimistično. Drago joj je što se to promijenilo, jer ljudi sve više postaju svjesni da je hrana jako bitna.

Kao dokaz navodi primjer od prije više od trideset godina. Maslinari su tada dolazili s pitanjem kako dobiti visokokvalitetno maslinovo ulje. Prema njezinim riječima, znalo se da su hrvatske masline kvalitetnije i zdravije od maslina drugih mediteranskih zemalja, zahvaljujući **specifičnoj mikroklimi od Istre do Dubrovnika**.

Maslinari su ipak bili skeptični i masline su stavljali **u more kako bi se odgorčale**. Gošća objašnjava zašto je to bila velika pogreška. Plod u slanoj vodi gubi vodu i smežura se, a u toj su vodi upravo **biofenoli**, najkvalitetnije tvari u maslini. S vodom bi izašli i najvrjedniji sastojci.

Naglašava da je promjena trajala dugo i da nije bila samo njezina zasluga. Bila je to, kako kaže, "vojska ljudi" koja je o tome govorila i pisala, uključujući brojne doktorate. Rezultat je vidljiv: danas hrvatska maslinova ulja postižu vrhunske rezultate i ubrajaju se među najkvalitetnija.

Gošća vjeruje da će se jednako tako, s vremenom, promovirati i svijest o tome što stavljamo na tanjur, koliko jedemo i kako organiziramo svakodnevnu prehranu. Pritom naglašava da ne treba biti **ortoreksičan ni opsjednut hranom**, nego se oslanjati na ono što je dostupno i nije preskupo.
sections.subtitle_en: The lesson of Croatian olive oil: from olives in the sea to top awards
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how olive growers used to debitter olives in the sea
sections.content_en:
When asked whether people underestimate the importance of nutrition for health, Donatella Verbanac answers optimistically. She is glad that this has changed, because people are increasingly becoming aware that food is very important.

As proof, she cites an example from more than thirty years ago. Olive growers then came with the question of how to obtain high-quality olive oil. According to her words, it was known that Croatian olives were of higher quality and healthier than the olives of other Mediterranean countries, thanks to the **specific microclimate from Istra to Dubrovnik**.

Yet the olive growers were skeptical and put the olives **into the sea in order to debitter them**. The guest explains why that was a big mistake. In salt water the fruit loses water and shrivels, and in that water are precisely the **biophenols**, the highest quality substances in the olive. With the water, the most valuable ingredients would also exit.

She emphasizes that the change took a long time and was not only her merit. It was, as she says, an "army of people" that spoke and wrote about it, including numerous doctorates. The result is visible: today Croatian olive oils achieve top results and are counted among the highest quality.

The guest believes that in the same way, over time, awareness will also be promoted about what we put on our plate, how much we eat, and how we organize our daily diet. At the same time, she emphasizes that one should not be **orthorexic or obsessed with food**, but rely on what is available and not too expensive.

sections.subtitle: Zdravovječnost umjesto dugovječnosti: stol i krevet spajaju ljude
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac pohvaljuje pojam 'zdravovječnost'
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac ističe da se jednostavno i kvalitetno može jesti, i da prehrana tako može postati najbolji saveznik u onome što naziva **zdravovječnošću**. Svjesno odbacuje pojam dugovječnosti, jer cilj nije samo dug život, nego sačuvati relativno solidno i pristojno zdravlje.

Pojam pripisuje podcastu i Sebastianu. Voditelj odmah potvrđuje da je zasluga Sebastianova, a ne njegova. Gošća priznaje da je izraz prvi put čula upravo u LOOD podcastu i dodaje: "Zdravovječnost, svaka čast."

Voditelj zatim spominje izjavu koju povezuje s njom: stol i krevet spajaju ljude. Gošća pojašnjava da misao nije njezina. Izrekla ju je kolegica iz Mađarske na kongresu gastroenterologa, koji se, koliko se sjeća, održao u Opatiji početkom 2000-ih. Prema toj misli, dvije su stvari u kući koje spajaju ljude: **stol i krevet**. Gošća se s tim slaže i kaže da je to istina.
sections.subtitle_en: Healthspan instead of longevity: table and bed bring people together
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac praises the term 'healthspan'
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac points out that one can eat simply and with quality, and that nutrition can thus become the best ally in what she calls **healthspan**. She consciously rejects the concept of longevity, because the goal is not merely a long life, but preserving relatively solid and decent health.

She attributes the term to the podcast and to Sebastian. The host immediately confirms that the credit belongs to Sebastian, and not to him. The guest admits that she heard the expression for the first time right on the LOOD podcast and adds: "Healthspan, hats off."

The host then mentions a statement that he associates with her: the table and the bed bring people together. The guest clarifies that the thought is not hers. It was uttered by a female colleague from Hungary at a congress of gastroenterologists, which, as far as she remembers, took place in Opatija in the early 2000s. According to that thought, there are two things in the house that bring people together: **the table and the bed**. The guest agrees with this and says that it is the truth.

sections.subtitle: Bez ortoreksije: kuhanje kao čin okupljanja obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o tome kako hranom okuplja obitelj oko stola
sections.content:
Voditelj otvoreno priznaje da je perfekcionist. Sve mora izvagati i sve mora biti na svom mjestu, pa ponekad upada u svojevrsnu **ortoreksiju**. Kaže da nakon svakog razgovora s Donatellom Verbanac osjeti "nalet ljepote" drugačijeg, optimističnijeg, opuštenijeg i jednostavnijeg odnosa prema hrani. Zamoli je da tu filozofiju prenese slušateljima.

Gošća odgovara da ima sreću što voli kuhati i pripremati hranu, ali nije opsjednuta time. Smatra da obitelj to razumije, jer ih upravo tako **okuplja oko stola**. Kad je obitelj na okupu, zajednički obrok postaje ono što svi dijele.

Ipak, nastoji što više namirnica pripremiti sama, kako bi mogla kontrolirati što jede. Tu dolazi do teme koja joj je posebno draga, fermentirane hrane.
sections.subtitle_en: Without orthorexia: cooking as an act of gathering the family
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about how she gathers her family around the table with food
sections.content_en:
The host openly admits that he is a perfectionist. Everything has to be weighed and everything has to be in its place, so he sometimes falls into a kind of **orthorexia**. He says that after every conversation with Donatella Verbanac he feels a "rush of beauty" of a different, more optimistic, more relaxed, and simpler relationship toward food. He asks her to convey that philosophy to the listeners.

The guest replies that she is fortunate to love cooking and preparing food, but she is not obsessed with it. She believes that her family understands this, because that is precisely how she **gathers them around the table**. When the family is together, the shared meal becomes what everyone shares.

Nevertheless, she strives to prepare as many foodstuffs as possible herself, so that she can control what she eats. Here she comes to a topic that is particularly dear to her, fermented food.

sections.subtitle: Moć fermentacije: kiseli kupus, kefir i ukiseljene lubenice s osječke tržnice
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac opisuje ukiseljeno povrće s osječke tržnice
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac otkriva da kod kuće ima **mnogo fermentirane hrane** i da je bez problema sama priprema. Spominje kefir i kimchi, za koje kaže da su danas toliko dostupni da ih svatko može pripremiti.

Najviše pažnje ipak posvećuje **kiselom kupusu**. Navodi da je **Andrija Karačić** napravio doktorat na toj temi i pokazao da kiseli kupus ima značajne dobrobiti za metaboličko zdravlje. Studija je provedena na kontroliranoj skupini, koju su, koliko se gošća sjeća, činili hrvatski košarkaši reprezentativci. Dodaje da su slične učinke pokazali i ljudi iz kultura u kojima kiseli kupus nije dio tradicionalne prehrane.

U Hrvatskoj je to, naglašava, duboko ukorijenjena tradicija. Kupus i repa kiselili su se od Istre do Slavonije i Dalmacije. Ističe da takva hrana nije samo za zimu i da je izvrsna **comfort food** u svako doba godine. Prije svega nudi peti okus, **umami**. Kiseli kupus može se dodati u salatu, jesti s bučinim uljem ili sam, i uvijek je dobra salata.

Zatim se obraća voditelju, koji je odrastao u Slavoniji, i spominje "delicije" s **osječke tržnice**. Ondje kupuje od jednog gospodina ukiseljene paprike i ukiseljene male lubenice koje nisu uspjele narasti. Uz osmijeh dodaje da ih zapravo kiseli njegova supruga. To su, kaže, tradicije koje Hrvatska ima.

Gošća priznaje da je presretna kad ima takve namirnice doma. Svaki dan pije malo kefira i jede granolu koju sama radi.
sections.subtitle_en: The power of fermentation: sauerkraut, kefir, and pickled watermelons from the Osijek market
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac describes pickled vegetables from the Osijek market
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac reveals that at home she has **a lot of fermented food** and that she prepares it herself without any problem. She mentions kefir and kimchi, which she says are today so accessible that anyone can prepare them.

Most attention, however, she devotes to **sauerkraut**. She states that **Andrija Karačić** did his doctorate on that topic and showed that sauerkraut has significant benefits for metabolic health. The study was conducted on a controlled group, which, as far as the guest remembers, consisted of Croatian national basketball team players. She adds that similar effects were also shown by people from cultures in which sauerkraut is not part of the traditional diet.

In Croatia, she emphasizes, this is a deeply rooted tradition. Cabbage and turnip were pickled from Istra to Slavonija and Dalmacija. She points out that such food is not only for winter and that it is excellent **comfort food** at any time of the year. Above all, it offers the fifth taste, **umami**. Sauerkraut can be added to a salad, eaten with pumpkin seed oil or on its own, and it is always a good salad.

Then she turns to the host, who grew up in Slavonija, and mentions the "delicacies" from the **Osijek market**. There she buys from a gentleman pickled peppers and pickled small watermelons that did not manage to grow. With a smile she adds that actually his wife pickles them. Those are, she says, traditions that Croatia has.

The guest admits that she is overjoyed when she has such foodstuffs at home. Every day she drinks a little kefir and eats granola that she makes herself.

sections.subtitle: Hrvatska kao butik država
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća se obraća voditelju Vinku i govori o Hrvatskoj kao butik državi
sections.content:
Voditelj, potaknut pričom o tradicijskim namirnicama, primjećuje da bi Hrvatska mogla biti **gastronomski gigant** usporediv sa Španjolskom, Italijom i Francuskom. Ipak, čini mu se da tome ne posvećujemo dovoljno pažnje.

Donatella Verbanac se slaže i obraća mu se imenom: "Vinko, mi imamo takav potencijal da mi možemo biti ono što se kaže **butik država**, cijela, od početka do kraja." Svoju tvrdnju potkrepljuje nizom prednosti:

- **dobra edukacija** i kvalitetni ljudi,
- ljudi koji dobro govore strane jezike, osobito mlađe generacije koje se snalaze svugdje,
- **jedinstvene namirnice** za kojima bi drugi, kako kaže, bili "do neba zahvalni" kad bi ih imali.
sections.subtitle_en: Croatia as a boutique state
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest addresses the host Vinko and speaks about Croatia as a boutique state
sections.content_en:
The host, prompted by the story about traditional foodstuffs, observes that Croatia could be a **gastronomic giant** comparable to Spain, Italy, and France. Yet, it seems to him that we do not devote enough attention to this.

Donatella Verbanac agrees and addresses him by name: "Vinko, we have such potential that we can be what is called a **boutique state**, the whole thing, from beginning to end." She supports her assertion with a series of advantages:

- **good education** and quality people,
- people who speak foreign languages well, especially the younger generations who manage everywhere,
- **unique foodstuffs** for which others, as she says, would be "grateful to heaven" if they had them.

sections.subtitle: Istarski stol kao povijesni zemljovid: od križarskih ratova do Austro-Ugarske
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac objašnjava povijesne utjecaje na istarsku kuhinju
sections.content:
Voditelj nabraja regionalnu raznolikost: Istra, Dalmacija, Slavonija, središnja Hrvatska i Lika. Gošća dodaje Gorski kotar i cijelu obalu. Spominje da se na **Rabu** suše ribe, a na **Lošinju** menulice, što je prema njezinim riječima tradicija naučena još u vrijeme križarskih ratova.

Prisjeća se izraza koji koriste neki Istrijani, **položajna renta**. Hrvatska je, naime, zbog svog položaja uvijek bila "na putu svima". Gošća to okreće na dobro: od svih koji su ovuda prolazili moglo se nešto lijepo i dobro naučiti.

To najbolje vidi u istarskoj kuhinji, u kojoj se utjecaji isprepliću. Gostima sa sjevera Europe teško je objasniti zašto se na istom stolu nalaze:

- tjestenina,
- sarme,
- punjene paprike "kao da si u Mađarskoj",
- fritule ili slatki raviolni koji nemaju veze s talijanskim raviolima.

Objašnjava da je to ostavština **Austro-Ugarske**, pa čak i turskih vremena. Navodi i primjer Orlića, koji su u okolicu Peroja došli bježeći pred Turcima. Zaključuje da gotovo svaka općina u Hrvatskoj ima nešto svoje, a uz smijeh dodaje da općina danas ima i previše.
sections.subtitle_en: The Istrian table as a historical map: from the Crusades to Austria-Hungary
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac explains historical influences on Istrian cuisine
sections.content_en:
The host enumerates regional diversity: Istra, Dalmacija, Slavonija, central Croatia, and Lika. The guest adds Gorski kotar and the entire coast. She mentions that on **Rab** fish are dried, and on **Lošinj** picarels, which according to her words is a tradition learned as far back as the time of the Crusades.

She recalls an expression used by some Istrians, **positional rent**. Croatia, namely, because of its position was always "in everyone's way". The guest turns this to the good: from everyone who passed through here, something beautiful and good could be learned.

She sees this best in Istrian cuisine, in which influences intertwine. For guests from northern Europe it is difficult to explain why on the same table there are:

- pasta,
- sarma (cabbage rolls),
- stuffed peppers "as if you were in Hungary",
- fritule or sweet ravioli that have nothing to do with Italian ravioli.

She explains that this is a legacy of **Austria-Hungary**, and even Turkish times. She also cites the example of the Orlić family, who came to the vicinity of Peroj fleeing from the Turks. She concludes that almost every municipality in Croatia has something of its own, and with a laugh adds that today there are even too many municipalities.

sections.subtitle: Jadranska prehrana, egzotično voće iz Zagorja i zaboravljeni nasadi badema
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o zapuštenim nasadima badema i oraha u Hrvatskoj
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac ponavlja jednu od središnjih ideja razgovora. Hrvatska bi trebala šire i bolje promovirati **jadransku prehranu**, a ne samo općenitu mediteransku, koja obuhvaća šesnaestak zemalja Mediterana.

Ističe i klimatske promjene. Zbog toplinskih promjena danas se lijepo uzgajaju namirnice i u **Zagorju**. Na zagrebačkom **Kvatriću** svakog petka održava se plac na kojem ljudi prodaju egzotično voće uzgojeno u Hrvatskoj.

Posebno je žalosti sudbina koštunjavog voća. Hrvatska je nekad imala jako dobre nasade **badema i oraha**, a sada se čini kao da je ta proizvodnja nestala. Možda nije isplativa, priznaje, ali mnogo zemljišta ostaje neposađeno. Pita se zašto ga ne bismo iskoristili.
sections.subtitle_en: The Adriatic diet, exotic fruit from Zagorje, and forgotten almond plantations
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about abandoned almond and walnut plantations in Croatia
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac repeats one of the central ideas of the conversation. Croatia should more broadly and better promote the **Adriatic diet**, and not only the general Mediterranean one, which encompasses some sixteen Mediterranean countries.

She also points out climate change. Due to thermal changes, today foodstuffs are grown nicely in **Zagorje** as well. At Zagreb's **Kvatrić**, every Friday a market is held where people sell exotic fruit grown in Croatia.

She is particularly saddened by the fate of tree nuts. Croatia once had very good **almond and walnut** plantations, and now it seems as though that production has disappeared. Perhaps it is not profitable, she admits, but a lot of land remains unplanted. She wonders why we shouldn't make use of it.

sections.subtitle: Čarobni štapić: prestanimo kukati i promijenimo stav
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac poručuje ljudima da prestanu kukati
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja hipotetsko pitanje. Kad bi gošća imala čarobni štapić za cijelu Hrvatsku i regiju, odakle podcast prati mnogo ljudi, što bi im poručila kako bi postigli ne samo dugovječnost nego i zdravovječnost?

Odgovor Donatelle Verbanac je izravan: **da se okrenu sami sebi i jednostavno prestanu kukati.** Smatra da od plakanja nad sudbinom nema koristi. Plakati bi se eventualno moglo nad epigenetskim promjenama, ali ako se o njima prestane razmišljati, dodaje, možda se neće ni ispoljiti.

Govori o **snazi misli i stava**, jer čovjek živi onu stvarnost koju u sebi stalno projicira. Najgore u hrvatskom mentalitetu, prema njezinu mišljenju, jest stalno žaljenje i čekanje da netko drugi osigura bolji život. Postavlja pitanje što bi uopće značio bolji život. Ovdje se živi sasvim pristojno i dobro. Odgovorno tvrdi, jer je mnogo putovala, da je teško naći zemlju s toliko ljepote na jednom mjestu. Uz to, Hrvatska ima dobro educirane i pametne ljude. Poruka je jasna: **uzmi stvar u svoje ruke.**
sections.subtitle_en: A magic wand: let us stop complaining and change our attitude
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac tells people to stop complaining
sections.content_en:
The host asks a hypothetical question. If the guest had a magic wand for all of Croatia and the region, from where many people follow the podcast, what would she tell them so that they achieve not only longevity but also healthspan?

Donatella Verbanac's answer is direct: **that they turn to themselves and simply stop complaining.** She believes that there is no use in crying over destiny. One could eventually cry over epigenetic changes, but if one stops thinking about them, she adds, perhaps they will not even manifest.

She speaks about the **power of thought and attitude**, because a person lives that reality which they constantly project within themselves. The worst thing in the Croatian mentality, in her opinion, is constant whining and waiting for someone else to secure a better life. She asks the question of what a better life would even mean. People live quite decently and well here. She responsibly claims, because she has traveled a lot, that it is hard to find a country with so much beauty in one place. In addition, Croatia has well-educated and smart people. The message is clear: **take matters into your own hands.**

sections.subtitle: Hrabrost za promjenu i gradski vrt od 50 kvadrata
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća priča o svom gradskom vrtu od 50 kvadrata
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac kao svijetli primjer navodi samog voditelja. Mlad čovjek imao je stabilan posao i stabilan dohodak, a usudio se zakoračiti u nepoznato kako bi ostvario ono što želi i provjerio je li za to sposoban. "Svaka ti čast na tome", poručuje mu. Dodaje da to svatko može, "sto puta".

Izlaže i vlastito iskustvo. S cijelom obitelji više je puta mijenjala mjesta u kojima je živjela i radna mjesta. Naglašava da **djeca vide primjer roditelja**. Onaj tko je usredotočen na svoj cilj nema vremena žaliti se ni tugovati. Savjetuje da se najprije promijeni stav, a onda će se, kaže, sve početi mijenjati.

Kao dokaz da se može mnogo toga navodi svoj **gradski vrt od 50 kvadrata**, koji je dobila 2015. godine. Rodni grad napustila je davne 1980., kad je došla studirati u Zagreb, i nikad se nije trajno vratila. O vrtlarstvu je znala onoliko koliko je pohvatala kao dijete. Ipak, ove godine nije morala ići ni na plac. Na tih 50 kvadrata uvijek ima dovoljno za salatu, a stane i malo graška.
sections.subtitle_en: Courage for change and a 50-square-meter city garden
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest talks about her 50-square-meter city garden
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac cites the host himself as a bright example. A young man had a stable job and a stable income, and dared to step into the unknown in order to achieve what he wants and check whether he is capable of it. "Hats off to you for that", she tells him. She adds that anyone can do that, "a hundred times".

She also presents her own experience. With her entire family, she changed the places where she lived and workplaces multiple times. She emphasizes that **children see the example of their parents**. Whoever is focused on their goal has no time to complain or mourn. She advises to first change one's attitude, and then, she says, everything will begin to change.

As proof that much can be done, she cites her **50-square-meter city garden**, which she received in 2015. She left her hometown back in 1980, when she came to study in Zagreb, and never returned permanently. About gardening she knew as much as she picked up as a child. Still, this year she didn't even have to go to the market. In those 50 square meters there is always enough for a salad, and a few peas also fit.

sections.subtitle: Povrće na terasi po uzoru na susjeda iz Praga
sections.screenshot_description: Donatella Verbanac opisuje vrt u stiroporima na terasi u Njivicama
sections.content:
Svjesna da nema svatko mogućnost dobiti komad zemlje, Donatella Verbanac podsjeća da i u stanu postoje rješenja. Dok je živjela u Njivicama, na otvorenoj krovnoj terasi imali su tegle u kojima su sadili povrće.

Ideju, naglašava, nije sama izmislila. Preuzela ju je od susjeda, gradskog djeteta i inženjera iz **Praga** koji je radio na Krku i bio oženjen Hrvaticom. On je donio kulturu prema kojoj se na dobroj terasi treba nešto posaditi. U tadašnjoj Čehoslovačkoj ljudi su, kaže, bili odgojeni tako da nijedan komad zemlje ni komadić sunca ne smije ostati prazan ako ondje nešto može rasti.

Živjeli su u poluspojenim kućicama. Na drugom katu bila je poluzatvorena terasa sa sušionom i vodom te otvoreni dio na kojem su u velikim stiroporima uzgajali povrće. Gošća je iz Istre donosila sjeme i sadnice radiča. Uvijek su imali malo radiča, peršina i rajčice, a susjed je uzgajao čak i patlidžane.
sections.subtitle_en: Vegetables on the terrace modeled after a neighbor from Prague
sections.screenshot_description_en: Donatella Verbanac describes a garden in Styrofoam boxes on the terrace in Njivice
sections.content_en:
Aware that not everyone has the opportunity to get a piece of land, Donatella Verbanac reminds that solutions also exist in an apartment. While she lived in Njivice, on the open roof terrace they had pots in which they planted vegetables.

The idea, she emphasizes, she did not invent herself. She took it over from a neighbor, a city child and engineer from **Prague** who worked on Krk and was married to a Croatian woman. He brought the culture according to which on a good terrace something should be planted. In the then Czechoslovakia people were, she says, brought up so that no piece of land nor bit of sunshine must remain empty if something can grow there.

They lived in semi-detached houses. On the second floor there was a semi-enclosed terrace with a drying area and water, and an open part where they grew vegetables in large Styrofoam boxes. The guest brought radicchio seeds and seedlings from Istra. They always had a little radicchio, parsley, and tomatoes, and the neighbor even grew eggplants.

sections.subtitle: Ljubav, dobrota i odbacivanje negativnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o širenju pozitivne energije i dobrote
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac zaključuje da svatko tko ima koliko-toliko zdrava osjetila i može se kretati nema razloga za očaj. Ljude s invaliditetom i hendikepom naziva **herojima i najvećim borcima**, a osobito to vrijedi za njihove roditelje i skrbnike. Primjećuje da takvi ljudi rijetko očajavaju.

Njezina je poruka: samo naprijed, hrabro, i širiti pozitivne misli. Neka svaki atom čovjeka i nakon njegove dezintegracije bude okružen pozitivnom energijom, u smislu širenja dobrote. Poziva se na akademkinju Vidu de Marin i na **ljubav** kao strahovito važan korak u ljudskoj egzistenciji. Čovjeka naziva najsavršenijim bićem, kakvom sličnog u svemiru još nema, i poziva da se cijeni ono što imamo.

Podsjeća da Hrvatska nema ni četiri milijuna stanovnika i ponavlja da je upravo zato **butik država**. Poziva da se riješimo negativnosti i nikome ne naudimo, jer se slično sličnim privlači. Tko je dobar, privući će dobre ljude, a to se dalje samo širi. Voditelj se slaže da stav definitivno treba korigirati.
sections.subtitle_en: Love, goodness, and casting off negativity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about spreading positive energy and goodness
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac concludes that anyone who has more or less healthy senses and can move has no reason for despair. She calls people with disabilities and handicaps **heroes and the greatest fighters**, and this is especially true for their parents and caregivers. She observes that such people rarely despair.

Her message is: just onward, courageously, and spread positive thoughts. May every atom of a human being, even after their disintegration, be surrounded by positive energy, in the sense of spreading goodness. She refers to academician Vida Demarin and to **love** as a tremendously important step in human existence. She calls man the most perfect being, the likes of which does not yet exist in the universe, and calls for appreciating what we have.

She reminds that Croatia does not even have four million inhabitants and repeats that precisely because of this it is a **boutique state**. She calls for getting rid of negativity and harming no one, because like attracts like. Whoever is good will attract good people, and that just spreads further. The host agrees that the attitude definitely needs to be corrected.

sections.subtitle: Mirovina za tjedan dana i ideja o emisiji o hrani
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita Donatellu Verbanac o planovima za mirovinu
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj pita što će Donatella Verbanac raditi u mirovini, u koju odlazi za tjedan dana. Predlaže joj vlastitu TV emisiju u kojoj bi kuhala, govorila o hrani i učila i inspirirala gledatelje.

Gošća se našali da kulinarskih emisija ima dosta. Voditelj inzistira da bi njezina bila posebna. Ona ostavlja vrata otvorenima i kaže da se uvijek mogu dogovarati, ali najprije se želi resetirati i odmoriti. To ne znači da se neće ničim baviti. Želi pustiti da joj stvari dođu same.

Priznaje da će tempo morati malo prilagoditi, ali nije nezadovoljna kako sada ide. Naglašava da mora biti zahvalna na svemu što ima.
sections.subtitle_en: Retirement in a week and the idea of a food show
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks Donatella Verbanac about plans for retirement
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, the host asks what Donatella Verbanac will do in retirement, into which she is going in a week. He suggests to her her own TV show in which she would cook, talk about food, and teach and inspire viewers.

The guest jokes that there are plenty of culinary shows. The host insists that hers would be special. She leaves the door open and says that they can always agree, but first she wants to reset and rest. That does not mean she will not be engaged in anything. She wants to let things come to her on their own.

She admits that she will have to adjust the pace a little, but she is not dissatisfied with how it is going now. She emphasizes that she must be grateful for everything she has.

sections.subtitle: Poruka četrdesetogodišnjacima, knjiga 'Volim gorko' i 65. rođendan
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća se prisjeća svoje 40. godine i knjige 'Volim gorko'
sections.content:
Donatella Verbanac obraća se generaciji četrdesetogodišnjaka, kojoj pripada i voditelj. Sjeća se da je sebi, kad je napunila 40 godina, rekla: **"Sad je čas."** Imala je snagu prihvatiti svaki posao koji joj se ponudi i probati što više toga.

Odlučila je da će s 50 godina malo stati. Tada je objavila svoju treću knjigu, **"Volim gorko"**, i proslavila 50. rođendan. Kaže da joj se čini kao da je to bilo jučer, a za dva mjeseca puni 65 godina. Ta će proslava, dodaje, biti malo drugačija.
sections.subtitle_en: A message to forty-year-olds, the book 'I Love Bitter', and the 65th birthday
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls her 40th year and the book 'I Love Bitter'
sections.content_en:
Donatella Verbanac addresses the generation of forty-year-olds, to which the host also belongs. She remembers that when she turned 40, she said to herself: **"Now is the time."** She had the strength to accept any job offered to her and to try as much as possible.

She decided that at 50 she would pause a little. Then she published her third book, **"I Love Bitter"**, and celebrated her 50th birthday. She says that it seems to her as if that were yesterday, and in two months she turns 65. That celebration, she adds, will be a little different.

sections.subtitle: Sljedeća godina bit će još bolja: oproštaj nakon trećeg gostovanja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj i Donatella Verbanac zahvaljuju jedno drugome na kraju razgovora
sections.content:
Voditelj se prisjeća poruke koju mu je gošća poslala, u kojoj stoji da će sljedeća godina biti još bolja od ove. Ona to i ponavlja: **"Sljedeća godina bit će još bolja."** Voditelj priznaje da mu se njezin optimizam jako sviđa.

Zahvaljuje joj od srca na **trećem gostovanju** u podcastu i šali se da će uskoro postati domaćin, a ne gost. Zahvaljuje i na svim lekcijama koje je podijelila sa slušateljima.

Donatella Verbanac uzvraća da je vrijeme prošlo u trenu i zahvaljuje na pozivu. Poručuje voditelju da ga prati i podržava, da kreće u jako dobrom smjeru te mu zahvaljuje na hrabrosti. Zaključuje da je on dobar primjer svim mladima.
sections.subtitle_en: Next year will be even better: farewell after the third guest appearance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and Donatella Verbanac thank each other at the end of the conversation
sections.content_en:
The host recalls a message the guest sent him, which says that next year will be even better than this one. She repeats it as well: **"Next year will be even better."** The host admits that he really likes her optimism.

He thanks her from the heart for her **third guest appearance** on the podcast and jokes that she will soon become the host, not the guest. He also thanks her for all the lessons she shared with the listeners.

Donatella Verbanac replies that time passed in an instant and thanks him for the invitation. She tells the host that she follows and supports him, that he is heading in a very good direction, and thanks him for his courage. She concludes that he is a good example to all young people.
